projects.content:
## Overview

Ian Xiaohei Illustrations is a Codex Skill that guides AI agents to generate body illustrations for Chinese articles, posts, blogs, Notion documents, and methodology content\. It is not a generic illustration prompt or a PPT infographic template\. Its core approach is to first understand cognitive anchors in an article, then turn one judgment, process, structure, state, or metaphor into a memorable 16:9 hand\-drawn explainer image\. The default visual IP is Xiaohei: a solid black character with white dot eyes, thin legs, and a blank expression that must take part in how the system works\. It is made by Ian, a product designer exploring possibilities for tomorrow\.

## Key Features

- Default output is 16:9 horizontal body illustrations and a 4\-8 image shot list for an article\. Each image includes a theme, core meaning, structure type, Xiaohei action, and Chinese annotation suggestions; final PNGs are saved to the workspace's assets folder in an illustrations

## Use Cases

- Writing Chinese articles, posts, blogs, Notion documents, or methodology content that needs body illustrations and article visuals\. Creating knowledge content, methodology content, or AI workflow content and wanting to turn abstract judgments into concrete metaphors\. Using Codex

## Getting Started

- Clone the ian\-xiaohei\-illustrations repository and enter the directory\. Copy the ian\-xiaohei\-illustrations subdirectory from the repository into the Codex skills directory, for example $\{CODEX\_HOME:\-$HOME/\.codex\}/skills/\. After installation, call $ian\-xiaohei\-illustrations in

## Deployment & Requirements

- The subdirectory ian\-xiaohei\-illustrations/ in the repository is what needs to be installed into Codex\. The installation location is $\{CODEX\_HOME:\-$HOME/\.codex\}/skills/\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

Ian Xiaohei Illustrations 是一个 Codex Skill，用来指导 AI Agent 为中文文章、帖子、博客、Notion 文档和方法论内容生成正文配图。它不是通用插画 prompt，也不是 PPT 信息图模板，核心是先理解文章里的认知锚点，再把其中一个判断、流程、结构、状态或隐喻，变成一张有记忆点的 16:9 手绘解释图。默认视觉 IP 是“小黑”：黑色实心、白点眼、细腿、空表情的小角色，必须参与系统运转。

## 核心功能

- 默认输出 16:9 横版正文配图，并为一篇文章生成 4\-8 张 shot list。
- 每张图包含主题、核心意思、结构类型、小黑动作和中文标注建议，最终 PNG 保存到 workspace 的 assets 目录下以文章 slug 命名的 illustrations 文件夹。
- 默认视觉风格为纯白背景、黑色手绘线稿、大量留白、少量红橙蓝中文手写批注，主体约占画面 40%\-60%。
- 每张图只表达一个核心动作、结构、状态或隐喻，小黑必须参与核心动作。
- 工作流程包括提炼认知锚点、选择结构类型、重新发明物理隐喻、逐张调用图像模型生成并按 QA checklist 检查。
- 支持只做配图规划、直接生成正文配图、为单个概念生成一张图，以及编辑已有图片去掉标题或错误文字。

## 适用场景

- 写中文文章、帖子、博客、Notion 文档或方法论内容，需要正文配图和文章插图。
- 做知识型内容、方法论内容、AI 工作流内容，希望把抽象判断画成具体隐喻。
- 用 Codex 做内容生产，希望稳定复用一套视觉语言。
- 为单个概念生成一张正文配图，或编辑已有配图去掉标题/错误文字。

## 快速开始

projects.content:
## Overview

Inbox Zero is an AI email assistant and email client for Gmail, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Outlook accounts\. The assistant works in the background to organize your inbox, pre\-draft replies in your tone and style, and manage your calendar, while the email client offers a fast split\-inbox experience on web, desktop, and mobile\. It is open source, with the AI assistant, web app, and desktop email app published on GitHub, and it can also be self\-hosted for full control of your data\.

## Key Features

- AI personal assistant that organizes your inbox and pre\-drafts replies in your tone and style
- AI rules for email configured in plain English
- Reply Zero tracking of emails to reply to and those awaiting responses
- Bulk unsubscribe and bulk archive tools for cleaning up your inbox
- Cold email blocker that automatically blocks cold emails
- Email analytics that track your activity and trends over time

## Use Cases

- Individuals, entrepreneurs, and executives who want to buy back time spent on email
- Power users and teams handling high email volumes who need integrations and shared analytics
- Founders, small businesses, creators, realtors, customer support, and e\-commerce teams managing busy inboxes
- People who want to self\-host their email assistant and email client for full control

## Getting Started

- Use the hosted version of Inbox Zero at getinboxzero\.com
- Connect your Google or Microsoft email account; smart categories are set up automatically and you can use the provided categories or create your own
- Self\-host by running the one\-time setup wizard with npx @inbox\-zero/cli setup, then start containers with npx @inbox\-zero/cli start, and open http://localhost:3000
- Verify a Gmail or Outlook email account to link in two clicks and start organizing and drafting in minutes

## Deployment & Requirements

- Self\-hosting requires Docker and Node\.js v24 or later
- Self\-hosting via the CLI prerequisites are Docker and Node\.js v24\+; complete self\-hosting instructions, production deployment, OAuth setup, and configuration options are in the Self\-Hosting Docs
- Inbox Zero supports Gmail, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Outlook email accounts
- The iOS App Store app can connect to your own server URL if you self\-host

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The Android app is described as an older React Native app and is due for an update, so Android users may not have parity with the iOS app\.
- The iPhone app is not currently open source, though the project says it plans to open it; the AI assistant, web app, and desktop email app are open source\.
- Starting the AI assistant trial requires a credit card even though the email app itself is free to use\.

## Overview

Kilo Code is an open\-source AI coding agent and agentic engineering platform available in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, the CLI, cloud, Slack, and a desktop app\. It provides specialized agents, model selection across 500\+ models, and workflows for coding, planning, debugging, and code review\.

## Key Features

- Open\-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, CLI, cloud, Slack, and desktop\.
- 500\+ models with mid\-task switching and provider\-rate pricing with zero markup\.
- Specialized Code, Plan, Ask, and Debug agents, plus custom agents\.
- Auto Model routing with Efficient, Frontier, and Free options\.
- Kilo Marketplace for agents, skills, MCP servers, and plugins\.
- Autonomous mode for CI/CD through kilo run \-\-auto\.

## Use Cases

- Generate and edit code across multiple files from natural language\.
- Plan complex features and review implementation plans before coding\.
- Debug and trace issues in a codebase\.
- Run autonomous coding tasks in trusted CI/CD pipelines\.

## Getting Started

- Install the Kilo Code extension in VS Code or from the VS Code Marketplace, then create an account\.
- Install the CLI via npm, pnpm, bun, Homebrew, AUR, or the curl install script, then run kilo in a project directory\.
- Install the Kilo Code plugin from the JetBrains Marketplace or search for Kilo Code in Settings → Plugins\.
- Use the Cloud Agent from the web or set up automated code reviews for pull requests\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Kilo Desktop is marked as beta\.
- Autonomous mode auto\-approves permission prompts unless a rule denies the action and should only be used in trusted environments\.

projects.content:
## Overview

LangChain is a framework for building agents and LLM\-powered applications\. It provides create\_agent, a minimal, highly configurable agent harness\. The harness is everything around the model loop: the prompt, the tools, and any middleware that shapes behavior\. LangChain supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and more\. Its agents are built on top of LangGraph, and LangSmith can trace, debug, and evaluate agent behavior\.

## Key Features

- Standard model interface for chat models, embeddings, and more across providers, letting teams switch models with minimal code changes\.
- create\_agent provides a minimal, highly configurable harness composed from model, tools, prompt, and middleware\.
- Built on top of LangGraph, enabling durable execution, human\-in\-the\-loop support, persistence, and more\.
- LangSmith integration for tracing requests, debugging agent behavior, and evaluating outputs\.
- Real\-time data augmentation by connecting LLMs to diverse data sources and external or internal systems\.
- Model interoperability and rapid prototyping through a modular, component\-based architecture\.

## Use Cases

- Building agents and LLM\-powered applications\.
- Composing a customizable agent harness from model, tools, prompt, and middleware\.
- Connecting LLMs to diverse data sources and external or internal systems for real\-time data augmentation\.
- Swapping models across providers to find the best choice for application needs\.

## Getting Started

- Install LangChain with uv add langchain\.
- Initialize a chat model with init\_chat\_model and invoke it, for example with openai:gpt\-5\.5\.
- See the Installation instructions and Quickstart guide to start building agents and applications\.
- Use LangSmith to trace requests, debug agent behavior, and evaluate outputs by setting LANGSMITH\_TRACING=true and your API key\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Tracing, debugging, and evaluation capabilities rely on LangSmith and an API key, an external dependency for observability\.
- LangChain agents depend on LangGraph as the underlying orchestration layer for durable execution, human\-in\-the\-loop support, and persistence\.

## Overview

Langfuse is an open\-source platform for agent evals and observability\. It connects tracing, monitoring, datasets, experiments, and evaluation in one continuous loop, enabling teams to trace every LLM call, manage prompts, evaluate, and experiment from prototype to production scale\.

## Key Features

- Hierarchical traces capture every LLM call, tool invocation, and retrieval step, filterable by user, session, cost, latency, or custom metadata\.
- Evaluation with LLM\-as\-a\-judge, heuristic functions, or human review, run on production data or during experiments\.
- Prompt Management separates prompts from code with one\-click deployments and rollbacks\.
- Playground to test prompts on real production inputs and compare models side\-by\-side\.
- Experiments to define test cases, run experiments, and compare results side by side\.
- Cost & Latency monitoring with dashboards and automated alerts\.

## Use Cases

- Chat agents: session\-level tracing, evals, and cost visibility for chat support and assistant experiences\.
- Coding agents
- Workflow automation

## Getting Started

- Start by following the 'Get Started with Tracing' guide to ingest your first trace using OpenAI, LangChain, or the SDKs\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Self\-hosting is supported via Docker Compose, Kubernetes (Helm), and Terraform for AWS, GCP, and Azure\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

LCU exposes Codex's original computer\-use runtime to agent harnesses without requiring Codex authentication\. The official ChatGPT desktop app remains installed locally and supplies the runtime and instructions, while LCU handles setup and harness integration for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Pi, or custom clients\.

## Key Features

- Reads and controls desktop app windows: read windows, click, type, and take screenshots\.
- Provides opt\-in Chrome tab control through the official extension, with site approval\.
- Works with Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Pi, and offers a shared JavaScript client for other harnesses\.
- Uses the original runtime and byte\-identical instructions from the installed ChatGPT desktop app, preserving original approval prompts\.
- Supports Apple Silicon macOS and Linux on ARM64 or x86\-64\.
- Includes native app approval handling in Claude Code and macOS commands to list, allow, or revoke always\-allowed apps\.

## Use Cases

- Letting an agent read a Calendar window, type a note into TextEdit, save it, and open a repository in Chrome\.
- Adding computer\-use capabilities to an existing Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Pi workflow\.
- Running controlled Chrome tab operations only after enabling the official extension and approving sites\.
- Managing per\-app approvals on macOS from the terminal without opening the Codex app\.

## Getting Started

- Copy the installation prompt into your agent; it checks OS, architecture, and prerequisites, installs the latest release, and guides required permissions\.
- Restart the harness, ask it to use LCU to take a screenshot of a harmless window, and approve the request as a first check\.
- For manual installation, download the archive and matching checksum file for the machine, verify the checksum, extract it, and follow the installation guide\.
- On Apple Silicon macOS with Claude Code, add the LCU plugin marketplace and install lcu through the plugin manager\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Install the official ChatGPT desktop app first; it supplies the runtime and instructions, and LCU does not install it\.
- Install and sign in to a supported harness such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Pi\.
- For Codex CLI, update before setup to get the required mcp\_tool hook support\.
- On Apple Silicon macOS, approve Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions on first use\.
- On Linux ARM64 or x86\-64, use an Ubuntu 24\.04\-compatible glibc system with an active X11 desktop and D\-Bus\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Lightpanda is a headless browser engine written in Zig, built from scratch for automation, crawling, and AI agents\. It executes JavaScript without graphical rendering, offering a minimal memory footprint and high speed compared to traditional headless browsers like Chrome\.

## Key Features

- Built from scratch in Zig, not a Chromium fork\.
- Headless operation with JavaScript execution, no rendering overhead\.
- CDP and Webdriver Bidi support for Puppeteer and Playwright compatibility\.
- Agent mode with PandaScript for LLM\-driven browser automation\.
- Native MCP server with session isolation\.
- Benchmarked 9x faster and 16x less memory than headless Chrome\.

## Use Cases

- Web scraping and crawling at scale\.
- AI agent navigation and task automation\.
- Running Puppeteer/Playwright scripts with lower resource usage\.
- Server\-side page dumping to HTML, Markdown, PNG, or PDF\.

## Getting Started

- Install via curl script, Homebrew, Arch AUR, Docker, or nightly binaries\. Then run \./lightpanda fetch \-\-dump html \<url\> or start a CDP server with \./lightpanda serve\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Linux and macOS binaries available; Windows via WSL2\. Docker images for amd64 and arm64\. Linux binaries require glibc; musl\-based distros need a glibc base image\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Linux binaries are linked against glibc and fail on musl\-based distros like Alpine\.
- Telemetry is enabled by default and can be disabled via environment variable\.

projects.content:
## Overview

llama\.cpp enables LLM and VLM inference with minimal setup and state\-of\-the\-art performance on a wide range of hardware, locally and in the cloud\. It is built on top of the ggml library\.

## Key Features

- Plain C/C\+\+ implementation without any dependencies
- Optimized for Apple silicon via ARM NEON, Accelerate, and Metal frameworks
- Integer quantization from 1\.5\-bit to 8\-bit for faster inference and reduced memory use
- Custom CUDA kernels for NVIDIA GPUs, with AMD via HIP and Moore Threads via MUSA
- Vulkan and SYCL backend support
- CPU\+GPU hybrid inference for models larger than VRAM

## Use Cases

- Run LLM and VLM models locally from Hugging Face
- Launch an OpenAI\-compatible API server
- Use the built\-in web UI for interactive sessions
- Accelerate large models with hybrid CPU\+GPU inference

## Getting Started

- Visit https://llama\.app and follow the instructions
- Run with Docker (see Docker documentation)
- Download pre\-built binaries from the releases page
- Build from source by cloning the repository (see build guide)
- Example: llama cli \-hf ggml\-org/Qwen3\.5\-0\.8B\-GGUF

## Deployment & Requirements

- Supports a wide range of hardware backends including CPU, NVIDIA GPU (CUDA), AMD GPU (HIP), Apple Silicon (Metal), Intel GPU (SYCL), Vulkan, WebGPU, and more
- No external dependencies for the core implementation
- Can be deployed via Docker or pre\-built binaries

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The OpenVINO backend is marked as in progress, indicating incomplete support\.

projects.content:
## Overview

LobeHub is a platform that organizes your AI agents into 7×24 operations\. It acts as a Chief Agent Operator, hiring, scheduling, and reporting on your entire AI team\. The platform treats agents as the unit of work, offering a space where humans and agents co\-evolve\. It includes features for creating agents, collaborating in groups, and evolving personal memory\.

## Key Features

- Operator: Bring all your agents under one roof with an IM Gateway for chat\-based interaction\.
- Create: Agent Builder with auto\-configuration, unified access to any model, and 10,000\+ skills via MCP\-compatible plugins\.
- Collaborate: Agent Groups for parallel collaboration, Pages for shared context writing, Schedule for timed runs, Project organization, and Workspace for team visibility\.
- Evolve: Personal Memory with continual learning and white\-box, editable memory for transparency\.
- Self\-Hosting: Deploy via Vercel, Zeabur, Sealos, Alibaba Cloud, or Docker for private control\.

## Use Cases

- Managing a personal AI team across multiple models and tools in one unified workspace\.
- Automating scheduled tasks and workflows while you are away\.
- Collaborating with agents in shared workspaces for team projects and content creation\.
- Building custom agents with specific skills and memory for evolving needs\.

## Getting Started

- Deploy with one\-click on Vercel, Zeabur, Sealos, or Alibaba Cloud by providing your OpenAI API Key\. Alternatively, use Docker: create a folder, run the setup script, and start with docker compose up \-d\. For local development, clone the repo, run pnpm install, then pnpm dev for

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires an OPENAI\_API\_KEY environment variable for LLM access\. Optional variables include OPENAI\_PROXY\_URL for API proxy and OPENAI\_MODEL\_LIST for model customization\. Docker deployment needs a storage folder and the setup script from lobe\.li/setup\.sh\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Third\-party API proxies carry validity and security risks, as stated in the README disclaimer\.
- The plugin system is under active major development, with phases still being completed\.

projects.name: magpie
projects.tagline: Every agent's model. One place.
projects.taglineZh: 所有 agent 的模型，集中一处
projects.description: magpie is a menu bar app that lets you pick the model each AI coding agent uses, routing Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and others through one local gateway to providers such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM.
projects.descriptionZh: magpie 是一个菜单栏应用，让你为每个 AI 编码 agent 选择所用模型，并通过一个本地网关把 Codex、Claude Code、Gemini CLI 等 agent 的请求路由到 DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM 等服务商。
projects.content:
## Overview

magpie is a menu bar app and local gateway that lets you choose the model each AI coding agent uses\. It lists installed agents and their current models, rewrites the relevant config key when you pick another model, and routes requests through 127\.0\.0\.1:3425 so any agent can use any provider's model\.

## Key Features

- Menu bar panel lists each installed AI agent and its model; click a value to change it and magpie rewrites only that agent's key in its config file\.
- One local gateway at 127\.0\.0\.1:3425 translates OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, and Google Gemini APIs, including streaming, tool calls, and reasoning\.
- Surgical config edits preserve comments, ordering, and indentation in settings\.json, config\.toml, opencode\.jsonc, or config\.yaml; writes are atomic\.
- Signed\-in subscriptions from Claude Code, Codex/ChatGPT, and GitHub Copilot become providers that other agents can use without copying keys\.
- Provider presets and custom vendors are configured by pasting a key; model lists are fetched from the vendor and models\.dev, and keys stay in magpie\.
- Profiles snapshot every agent's settings, and routing groups can spread requests across multiple accounts or models with failover, rate\-limit, and quota handling\.

## Use Cases

- Run Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, and Gemini CLI on GLM from one menu bar picker\.
- Give OpenCode, Pi, Goose, or other agents access to a Claude Pro/Max or ChatGPT plan without pasting credentials into each agent\.
- Centralize vendor keys and base URLs in one local gateway so agents do not hold provider credentials\.
- Route requests across multiple accounts or keys to handle rate limits, quotas, and failover\.

## Getting Started

- Download the desktop app for Windows or macOS, or install from the terminal with the provided install script\.
- Add a provider with magpie provider add deepseek sk\-\.\.\.; a preset needs only the key, and local servers such as Ollama need none\.
- Assign models with commands such as magpie codex deepseek/deepseek\-v4\-pro, magpie claude moonshot/kimi\-k3, or magpie gemini zhipu/glm\-5\.3\.
- Use magpie tui for the terminal app, magpie ls to list agents and their models, and magpie save work followed by magpie use work for profiles\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon or Intel\.
- Windows 10 or later on x64 or ARM\.
- Linux with GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4\.1 on x86\-64 or ARM64\.
- Local gateway runs at 127\.0\.0\.1:3425; desktop app uses the system webview and is under 15 MB, with a 7 MB terminal\-only build\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- API keys must be added directly in magpie; it does not read keys from shell environment variables\.
- Vendor keys are kept in magpie and are not exposed to the agents it configures\.

projects.description: Mailcheap is a self-hosted newsletter app on Amazon SES. It includes an editor, list management, unsubscribe and bounce handling, stats, and a public archive. Costs about $0.10 per 1,000 emails.
projects.descriptionZh: Mailcheap 是一个基于 Amazon SES 的自托管邮件通讯应用，集编辑器、列表管理、退订与退信处理、统计和公开归档于一体。每发送 1,000 封邮件约花费 0.10 美元。
projects.content:
## Overview

Mailcheap is a self\-hosted newsletter app built on Amazon SES\. It provides an editor, list management, signup forms, unsubscribe handling, bounce and complaint handling, stats, and a public archive in one Next\.js app\. One admin, no teams, and your list stays in your database\. It costs about $0\.10 per 1,000 emails sent\.

## Key Features

- Editor with a live email preview, slash commands, image uploads, boxes, Markdown, and raw HTML\.
- Checks before every send: subject, preview text, unsubscribe link, size under Gmail's 100 KB clip, postal address, and verified domain\.
- Test emails, scheduling, and sending in batches through QStash at a configured rate, with step sending to engaged readers first\.
- Several newsletters in one install, each with its own from address, reply\-to, postal address, signup form, and signup API\.
- SES events, a shared suppression list, automatic send pausing when bounces pass 2% or complaints pass 0\.08%, one\-click unsubscribe, and optional list cleanup\.
- Public archive for each newsletter with issue pages, author page, share images, sitemap, optional custom domain, overview stats, and campaign reports by mailbox provider\.

## Use Cases

- Self\-hosting a newsletter while using your own Amazon SES account and keeping subscriber data in your own MongoDB database\.
- Running multiple newsletters from one install with separate send identities, signup forms, and archives\.
- Sending to the most engaged readers first and growing each send over time while monitoring deliverability\.
- Publishing issues on a public archive and measuring delivery, open, click, bounce, complaint, and provider\-level campaign performance\.

## Getting Started

- Plan for about an hour, most of it waiting for DNS and for AWS to approve production access\.
- Create a MongoDB Atlas cluster, add a database user with read and write access, allow 0\.0\.0\.0/0, and copy the connection string with a database name as MONGODB\_URI\.
- Deploy to Vercel or run on any Node\.js host with npm ci && npm run build && npm start behind HTTPS; set MONGODB\_URI, ADMIN\_EMAIL, ADMIN\_PASSWORD with 12\+ characters, and SESSION\_SECRET with 32\+ characters\.
- Configure Amazon SES by verifying a sending domain, setting a custom MAIL FROM domain, adding DMARC, requesting production access, creating a configuration set, creating an SNS topic, sending SES events to it, creating an IAM user, and adding SES\_REGION, SES\_ACCESS\_KEY\_ID,
- Set up QStash, add QSTASH\_TOKEN, QSTASH\_CURRENT\_SIGNING\_KEY, and QSTASH\_NEXT\_SIGNING\_KEY, create a newsletter, then set SENDING\_ENABLED=true and redeploy to turn sending on\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- MongoDB for contacts, campaigns, and stats; the free tier works\.
- Amazon SES for sending; about $0\.10 per 1,000 emails\.
- Upstash QStash for background sending and scheduling; free tier to start, then pay per message, and one message sends 50 emails\.
- Vercel or any Node\.js host for hosting; free tier works\.
- Optional Upstash Redis for rate limits shared by every server instance; free tier\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is a one\-time release with no support and no planned updates\.
- New Amazon SES accounts start in a sandbox limited to 200 emails per day and verified recipients only until production access is granted\.
- Without Redis, rate limits are counted per server instance and are not shared or persistent on serverless hosts, so Redis is recommended before placing a signup form on a busy site\.
- Background sending through QStash requires the app to be reachable on the internet\.
- Image uploads in the editor require optional Vercel Blob storage\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

Mailcheap 是一个基于 Amazon SES 构建的自托管邮件通讯应用。它在同一个 Next\.js 应用中提供编辑器、列表管理、注册表单、退订处理、退信与投诉处理、统计以及公开归档。只有一名管理员，无需团队协作，订阅者名单保存在你自己的数据库中。每发送 1,000 封邮件约花费 0\.10 美元。

## 核心功能

- 编辑器支持实时邮件预览、斜杠命令、图片上传、方框、Markdown 和原始 HTML。每次发送前会检查主题、预览文字、退订链接、大小是否低于 Gmail 的 100 KB 截断限制、邮寄地址和已验证域名。支持测试邮件、定时发送，以及通过 QStash 按设定速率分批发送，并可先发给最活跃的读者。一次安装可运行多个邮件通讯，每个都有自己的发件地址、回复地址、邮寄地址、注册表单和注册 API。包含 SES 事件、共享抑制列表，当退信率超过 2% 或投诉率超过 0\.08%

## 适用场景

- 在自己的 Amazon SES 账户上自托管邮件通讯，同时将订阅者数据保存在自己的 MongoDB 数据库中。一次安装运行多个邮件通讯，使用独立的发送身份、注册表单和归档。先向最活跃的读者发送，并随时间逐步增加发送量，同时监控送达率。将期号发布到公开归档，并衡量送达、打开、点击、退信、投诉以及各邮箱服务商层面的营销活动表现。

## 快速开始

- 预计需要约一小时，其中大部分时间用于等待 DNS 生效和 AWS 批准生产访问权限。创建 MongoDB Atlas 集群，添加具有读写权限的数据库用户，允许 0\.0\.0\.0/0，并将带数据库名称的连接字符串复制为 MONGODB\_URI。部署到 Vercel，或在任何 Node\.js 主机上以 npm ci && npm run build && npm start 运行并置于 HTTPS 之后；设置 MONGODB\_URI、ADMIN\_EMAIL、至少 12 个字符的 ADMIN\_PASSWORD，以及至少 32 个字符的

## 部署与要求

- MongoDB 用于存储联系人、营销活动和统计；免费套餐即可。Amazon SES 用于发送；每 1,000 封邮件约 0\.10 美元。Upstash QStash 用于后台发送和定时；初始可用免费套餐，之后按消息付费，一条消息可发送 50 封邮件。Vercel 或任何 Node\.js 主机用于托管；免费套餐即可。可选的 Upstash Redis 用于让所有服务器实例共享速率限制；免费套餐。

projects.content:
## Overview

Manufact is an MCP cloud platform for deploying, testing, observing, and publishing MCP servers and MCP apps\. It is built by the team behind the open\-source mcp\-use SDKs for TypeScript and Python and the open\-source MCP Inspector\. Deployments can originate from GitHub, the CLI, or Manufact's own MCP server, and the platform covers post\-deploy work such as cross\-client testing, MCP\-native analytics, and publishing checks for the ChatGPT Apps Store and Claude Cloud Connectors\.

## Key Features

- Deploy MCP servers and apps from GitHub, a template, or the CLI, with branch previews and custom domains\.
- Run cross\-client tests across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, and other clients, with LLM\-judged pass/fail results and CI gating\.
- Use the Cloud Inspector to trace, replay, and debug MCP traffic in production, and the open\-source MCP Inspector for tool testing, resource browsing, prompt testing, and JSON\-RPC logging\.
- Monitor MCP\-native analytics including tool calls, sessions, error rates, and p50/p95/p99 latency by tool, resource, and prompt\.
- Run publishing checks for the ChatGPT Apps Store and Claude Cloud Connectors, with fix guidance, E2E checks, and a generated submission pack\.
- Connect existing remote MCP servers by URL through the Manufact proxy to use chat, test suites, publish checks, and the submission pack without moving hosting\.

## Use Cases

- Teams deploying MCP servers or apps that need hosted endpoints, preview environments, and custom domains\.
- Developers validating MCP apps across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and other clients before marketplace submission\.
- Operators monitoring production MCP traffic, tool\-call volume, latency, errors, and session timelines\.
- Publishers preparing ChatGPT Apps Store or Claude Cloud Connectors listings with compliance checks and submission assets\.

## Getting Started

- Start with the mcp\-use SDK by running npx \-y create\-mcp\-use\-app@latest, then run npm run dev in the generated project and open the local Inspector path\.
- Deploy from GitHub by connecting the GitHub App, deploy from a template, or run npx mcp\-use deploy from the CLI\.
- Connect an existing remote MCP server by URL through the Manufact proxy to use testing and publishing features without moving hosting\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Deploy from GitHub, the CLI, Manufact's own MCP server, a template, or an existing remote MCP server connected by URL\.
- TypeScript and Python are first\-class through the mcp\-use SDKs, with presets for FastMCP and other frameworks, plus a Dockerfile option for anything else\.
- OAuth ships with Auth0, Better Auth, Clerk, Keycloak, Supabase, and WorkOS, plus custom providers that support dynamic client registration; clients connect with OAuth 2\.1 with PKCE or bearer tokens\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Marketplace publication is subject to OpenAI and Anthropic reviewing and approving their own listings\.
- Branch preview deployments are available only on the Hobby plan and above\.
- Existing mcp\-use v1 projects have a documented migration path\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Marble Skill Taxonomy is an open, structured taxonomy of what children learn across the primary/elementary years\. It decomposes learning into 1,590 fine\-grained micro\-topics across eight subjects, wires them into a directed acyclic prerequisite graph with 3,221 edges, aligns topics to national curriculum standards, and includes parent\-friendly domain summaries\.

## Key Features

- 1,590 micro\-topics, each with a plain\-language description, mastery evidence criteria, type, subject and domain, and approximate age range\.
- 3,221 prerequisite dependencies represented as a directed acyclic graph, with edges tagged hard or soft and carrying a one\-line reason\.
- Curriculum alignment linking micro\-topics to standards from NGSS, Common Core, the UK National Curriculum, and more\.
- 183 parent\-friendly one\-paragraph domain summaries per subject, domain, and age band\.
- Coverage across eight subjects: Science, Mathematics, English, History, Personal & Social Development, Life Skills, Computing, and Learning to Learn\.
- UTF\-8 JSON data files, JSON Schemas, and a manifest with counts and SHA\-256 checksums\.

## Use Cases

- AI tutoring and retrieval\-augmented generation systems that need structured curriculum knowledge\.
- Agent queries about what must be learned before a concept and what paths lead to a learning goal\.
- Knowledge\-gap diagnosis and personalized learning planning using assessment results and prerequisite relationships\.
- Curriculum analysis and exploration through a connected graph of learning topics\.

## Getting Started

- Load data/topics\.json and data/dependencies\.json as UTF\-8 JSON; no runtime or dependencies are required\.
- Build an ID map from topics and filter dependencies by topicId to retrieve prerequisites for a topic\.
- Validate structure and referential integrity with node scripts/validate\.mjs\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- No runtime or dependencies are required; the dataset is pure UTF\-8 JSON\.
- JSON Schemas are provided in schema/, and data/manifest\.json provides counts and SHA\-256 checksums\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: ODbL\-1\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Curriculum standards are extracted from third\-party frameworks, so users should account for the external origin of those standards\.
- The release deliberately omits semantic embeddings and any per\-child or user data\.

## Overview

Marketing Skills is a collection of AI agent skills focused on marketing tasks, built for technical marketers and founders\. It covers conversion optimization, copywriting, SEO, analytics, and growth engineering, and works with coding agents that support the Agent Skills spec\.

## Key Features

- 50 open\-source marketing skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other compatible agents\.
- Skills are markdown files that give AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows for marketing tasks\.
- The product\-marketing skill is the foundation; every other skill checks it first to understand product, audience, and positioning\.
- Skills reference each other and build on shared context across SEO and content, CRO, content and copy, paid and measurement, growth and retention, sales and GTM, and strategy\.
- Includes installation paths such as the npx skills CLI, Claude Code plugin, OpenAI Codex plugin, clone\-and\-copy, Git submodule, SkillKit, and Claude Web ZIPs\.
- Partner integrations include Converly for server\-side conversion tracking and Ploy for an AI website and growth platform\.

## Use Cases

- Technical marketers and founders can ask AI coding agents to help with conversion optimization, copywriting, SEO, analytics, and growth engineering\.
- Teams can install all skills or choose specific skills such as cro and copywriting for agent\-assisted marketing workflows\.
- Users can invoke skills directly, for example /cro, /emails, or /seo\-audit, when working on specific marketing tasks\.
- Agencies and service providers can run this work as a service, with Magister and Conversion Factory listed for done\-for\-you help\.

## Getting Started

- Install all skills with npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills\.
- Install specific skills with npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills \-\-skill cro copywriting\.
- Install via Claude Code plugin with /plugin marketplace add coreyhaines31/marketingskills and /plugin install marketing\-skills\.
- After installation, ask your agent to help with marketing tasks or invoke skills directly such as /cro, /emails, or /seo\-audit\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Works with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, and any agent that supports the Agent Skills spec\.
- For Claude Code the CLI installs into \.claude/skills/; universal agents share \.agents/skills/\.
- For Claude Web skill ZIPs, account permissions and code execution must allow skills\.
- The /plugin command is only available in an interactive Claude Code CLI session, not in Claude Code on the web, GitHub Actions, or other non\-interactive or remote environments\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Upgrading from v1\.x to v2\.0 can leave stale old\-name skill folders alongside the new skills, requiring manual cleanup\.
- The /plugin command is only available in an interactive Claude Code CLI session, so non\-interactive or remote environments need an alternative\.
- Installing a Claude Web skill ZIP does not configure local CLIs, MCP servers, credentials, or related skills\.
- The web\-target archive uses a shorter description, and its manifest may list skills whose description still needs review; release notes summarize omissions\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Mastra is an open\-source TypeScript framework for building AI\-powered applications and agents\. It provides agents, workflows, memory, workspaces, and observability, and integrates with frontend and backend frameworks such as React, Next\.js, and Node, or can run as a standalone server\.

## Key Features

- Agents use LLMs and tools to solve open\-ended tasks, reason about goals, decide which tools to use, and iterate until a final answer or optional stopping condition is met\.
- Graph\-based workflows orchestrate complex multi\-step processes with control flow methods such as \.then(), \.branch(), and \.parallel(), including human\-in\-the\-loop suspend and resume\.
- Memory and context management combine conversation history, retrieval from APIs, databases, and files, plus observational memory and semantic recall\.
- Built\-in observability includes evals, metrics, datasets, traces, and signals for inspecting and improving agent runs\.
- Model routing connects to multiple AI providers through one standard interface, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini\.
- Applications can deploy as a standalone Hono\-powered server, integrate with React, Next\.js, or Node, or use existing Hono, Express, or Fastify server apps\.

## Use Cases

- Conversational agents for customer support, onboarding, or internal queries\.
- Domain\-specific copilots for coding, legal, finance, research, or creative work\.
- Workflow automations that trigger, route, and complete multi\-step processes\.
- Decision\-support tools that analyze data and provide actionable recommendations\.

## Getting Started

- Create a project with npm create mastra@latest \<project\-name\> \-\- \-\-llm \<provider\>, choosing a supported provider such as openai, anthropic, google, or xai\.
- Enter the project directory and start the development server with npm run dev\.
- Open Mastra Studio at http://localhost:4111 to build, test, and manage agents, workflows, and tools\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Mastra applications can be deployed to any Node\.js\-compatible environment\.
- Optional built\-in deployers support Vercel, Netlify, and Cloudflare\.
- Deploy as a standalone server powered by Hono, integrate with Next\.js, or use an existing Hono, Express, Fastify, or other server app\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Human\-in\-the\-loop workflow pause and resume depends on storage to remember execution state\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

Mastra 是开源的现代 TypeScript 框架，用于构建 AI 驱动的应用与智能体。它提供智能体、工作流、记忆、工作区和可观测性；可与 React、Next\.js 和 Node 等前后端框架集成，也可作为独立服务器运行。

## 核心功能

- 智能体使用 LLM 和工具解决开放式任务，围绕目标推理、选择工具，并持续迭代，直到模型给出最终答案或满足可选停止条件。
- 基于图的工作流引擎通过 \.then()、\.branch() 和 \.parallel() 等方法控制复杂多步骤流程，并支持人工介入的暂停与恢复。
- 记忆与上下文管理结合对话历史、从 API、数据库和文件检索数据，以及观察式记忆和语义召回。
- 内置可观测性包括评估、指标、数据集、追踪和信号，用于检查并改进智能体运行。
- 模型路由通过统一接口连接多个 AI 提供商，包括 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Gemini 等。
- 应用可作为基于 Hono 的独立服务器部署，集成到 React、Next\.js 或 Node，也可接入现有 Hono、Express 或 Fastify 服务器应用。

## 适用场景

- 用于客户支持、用户引导或内部查询的对话式智能体。
- 面向编码、法律、金融、研究或创意工作的领域专用助手。
- 触发、路由并完成多步骤流程的工作流自动化。
- 分析数据并提供可执行建议的决策支持工具。

## 快速开始

- 使用 npm create mastra@latest \<项目名\> \-\- \-\-llm \<提供商\> 创建项目，提供商可选 openai、anthropic、google 或 xai。
- 进入项目目录后运行 npm run dev 启动开发服务器。
- 在本地 4111 端口打开 Mastra Studio，用于构建、测试和管理智能体、工作流与工具。

## 部署与要求

projects.descriptionZh: MCP for Blender 是一个开源 Blender 插件和 MCP 服务器，可将 Blender 3D 连接到任意 LLM，用于提示辅助建模、场景创建、对象与材质控制、可视化验证，以及资产和模型生成。该项目为社区插件，与 Blender Foundation 无隶属关系。
projects.content:
## Overview

MCP for Blender is an open source Blender addon and MCP server that lets an LLM control Blender through a socket\-based connection\. The AI can write Blender Python, create and modify objects, apply materials, inspect results through multiple views or renders, and search or import assets\. The project is a community plugin and is not affiliated with the Blender Foundation\.

## Key Features

- Two\-way communication between Blender and an LLM through a socket\-based server
- Create, modify, and delete 3D objects in Blender
- Apply and modify materials and colors
- Visual verification through viewport, camera, multi\-angle, wireframe, X\-ray, animation\-strip views, and renders
- Code execution where the AI writes Blender Python directly
- Asset and model generation using Poly Haven, Sketchfab, Poly Pizza, Tripo, Hyper3D Rodin, Hunyuan3D, and Meshy

## Use Cases

- Prompt\-assisted 3D modeling and scene creation
- Applying and modifying materials and colors
- Letting the AI inspect and verify its work with multi\-angle, camera, wireframe, X\-ray, animation\-strip views, and renders
- Importing assets or generating 3D models from supported sources

## Getting Started

- Run uvx mcp\-for\-blender setup if uv is already installed; otherwise use the one\-line installer for macOS/Linux or Windows\.
- Select which MCP clients to configure; setup adds a blender entry and saves a \.bak of each changed file\.
- Fully quit and reopen the AI app, open Blender, and ask it to build something\.
- For manual setup, install uv, add the MCP server to the client, run uvx mcp\-for\-blender install\-addon, enable Interface: MCP for Blender in Blender preferences, and start or connect the server\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Blender 3\.0 or newer
- Python 3\.10 or newer
- uv package manager, using the official installer rather than pip install uv
- An MCP client such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, OpenCode, or Antigravity
- Docker can host only the MCP server; Blender still runs on the host\. On Linux, use host networking and set BLENDER\_HOST to localhost\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The addon is an independent third\-party integration and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Blender Foundation\.
- The addon's socket server has no authentication or encryption\.
- By default, the AI can run any Python code in Blender\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Mem0 is a drop\-in memory infrastructure for AI agents and apps, providing persistent context that enables continuous learning from past user interactions\. It is built for production use\.

## Key Features

- Multi\-Level Memory: retains User, Session, and Agent state with adaptive personalization
- Memory Compression Engine: condenses chat history into compact memories to cut tokens and latency
- Single\-pass hierarchical distillation and multi\-signal retrieval (semantic, BM25, entity matching)
- Developer\-friendly: intuitive API, cross\-platform SDKs (Python, Node\.js), and managed service option
- Enterprise governance: SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR compliance, BYOK, zero\-trust, and portable deployment

## Use Cases

- AI Assistants: consistent, context\-rich conversations
- Customer Support: recall past tickets and user history for tailored help
- Healthcare: track patient preferences and history for personalized care
- Sales & CRM: track interactions, objections, and milestones across long sales cycles

## Getting Started

- Install the SDK with pip install mem0ai or npm install mem0ai\. For the cloud platform, sign up at app\.mem0\.ai and use the API key\. For self\-hosted, use docker compose up in the server directory\. The CLI is available via npm install \-g @mem0/cli or pip install mem0\-cli\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires an LLM (default OpenAI gpt\-5\-mini) and an embedding model (default text\-embedding\-3\-small)\. For hybrid search, a stronger embedding model like Qwen 600M is recommended\. Self\-hosted deployment requires Docker\. Python 3\.x or Node\.js is needed for SDK usage\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Open\-source SDK may not match managed platform performance\.
- Mem0 requires an external LLM to function\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open\-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems\. It lets AI applications connect to data sources, tools, and workflows, providing a standardized way to integrate capabilities\. The repository houses reference MCP server implementations and points to accompanying SDKs and community resources\.

## Key Features

- Open\-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems
- Enables AI applications to connect to data sources, tools, and workflows
- Standardized integration approach compared to a USB\-C port for AI applications
- Broad ecosystem support across AI assistants, development tools, and clients
- Reference servers demonstrate MCP features and official SDK usage
- SDKs available for languages including C\#, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift, and TypeScript

## Use Cases

- Agents can access Google Calendar and Notion to act as more personalized AI assistants
- Claude Code can generate a web app using a Figma design
- Enterprise chatbots can connect to multiple organizational databases for chat\-based data analysis
- AI models can create 3D designs on Blender and print them with a 3D printer

## Getting Started

- TypeScript\-based servers in the repository can be run directly with npx, such as npx \-y @modelcontextprotocol/server\-memory
- Python\-based servers can be run with uvx, such as uvx mcp\-server\-git, or installed with pip
- Servers should be configured into an MCP client; for example, Claude Desktop accepts mcpServers entries with command and args
- On Windows, npx\-based client entries should wrap npx with cmd /c

## Deployment & Requirements

- TypeScript servers require npx to run directly
- Python servers require uvx or pip
- An MCP client is needed to use a server in practice
- On Windows, npx commands must be wrapped with cmd /c

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The servers are reference implementations intended as educational examples, not production\-ready solutions\.
- Developers should evaluate security requirements and implement safeguards for their threat model\.
- Some reference servers are archived and may be replaced or maintained elsewhere\.

## Overview

Multica is a workspace that brings AI coding agents and human teammates together\. Agents are assigned issues, pick them up, work on a runtime you control, comment as they go, and hand results back for review\. The intent, run, decisions, and diff stay connected to the same issue, so context is never lost and nothing ships without human approval\.

## Key Features

- Works with 26 agent CLIs including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more\.
- Assign issues to agents like teammates; they pick up, report progress, and hand back for review\.
- Squads: put agents and people on one team with a leader routing work\.
- Skills: turn solved problems into reusable playbooks every agent can use\.
- Self\-host everything with Docker Compose or Helm on your own infrastructure\.
- Review gates ensure work lands in review, not main, so you decide what ships\.

## Use Cases

- Manage multiple AI coding agents in one workspace instead of separate terminal tabs\.
- Assign coding tasks to agents and track progress, blockers, and results\.
- Run automated standups, audits, and reports on a schedule with autopilots\.
- Self\-host for full control over data and infrastructure\.

## Getting Started

- Sign up at multica\.ai or download Multica Desktop for macOS, Windows, or Linux\. The desktop app automatically connects the computer it runs on as a runtime\. Ensure at least one supported agent CLI (like Claude Code or Codex) is installed and signed in on the machine that will

## Deployment & Requirements

- Self\-hosting requires Docker and pulls official images from GHCR\. The architecture uses Next\.js frontend, Go backend, and PostgreSQL 17\. For development, prerequisites include Node\.js 22, pnpm 10\.28\.2, Go 1\.26\.6, and Docker\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- iOS builds are available from source but not yet on the App Store\.
- The main branch moves quickly with frequent releases, so pull often\.

projects.content:
## Overview

NanoClaw is a secure, lightweight alternative to OpenClaw\. It runs your personal AI agent in isolated Docker containers, with a small codebase designed to be understood and customized\. It supports multiple messaging channels, scheduled tasks, and per\-agent workspaces, with credentials secured via a gateway\.

## Key Features

- Container isolation: every active session runs in its own Docker container\.
- Multi\-channel messaging: supports WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, and more, installed on demand\.
- Flexible isolation: connect each channel to its own agent or share one agent across channels\.
- Scheduled tasks: recurring jobs with optional script gates\.
- Credential security: agents never hold raw API keys; outbound requests route through a credential gateway\.
- Skills over features: add channels and providers via skills, keeping your fork lean\.

## Use Cases

- Personal AI assistant on messaging apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Slack\.
- Scheduled briefings and recurring tasks, such as morning news summaries\.
- Customized agent for individual workflows, with per\-agent group providers\.

## Getting Started

## Overview

Octop is an open\-source, self\-hosted AI assistant platform for households and small teams\. It runs a single process serving a web dashboard, CLI, IM channels, cron automation, and APIs, with all data under ~/\.octop/ on your own machine\.

## Key Features

- Multi\-user and multi\-agent operation with JWT authentication, per\-user agents, and an admin role\.
- Self\-hosted local\-first design that keeps config, chats, workspaces, and credentials on your machine\.
- Web dashboard, CLI, desktop client, and HTTP/SSE/WebSocket API access\.
- IM channels include Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, WeChat, Telegram, Discord, and WeCom\.
- Expert library, MBTI persona templates, expert sharing, and AgentTeams beta for multi\-step work\.
- Knowledge base RAG, plugins, connectors with OAuth and MCP, and ACP integration for IDE workflows\.

## Use Cases

- Personal assistant for weekly reports, notes, scheduling, and persistent memory\.
- Family sharing with one admin account and different agents or experts per member\.
- Team helper that bridges IM platforms and routes tasks into group chats\.
- Developer boost through ACP delegation to OpenCode or Claude Code, terminal AI, and browser automation\.

## Getting Started

- Install on macOS or Linux with the one\-line installer, or use PowerShell or cmd installers on Windows\.
- Run octop init to create the SQLite database, JWT secret, and first admin account under ~/\.octop/\.
- Run octop run, then open the web dashboard on local port 8088\.
- For production, Docker Compose is recommended; first boot creates the admin account and writes credentials to /data/\.octop/credential\.txt unless OCTOP\_DEFAULT\_PASSWORD is set\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Supported operating systems include macOS, Linux, and Windows\.
- No pre\-installed Python is required; the installer uses uv to provision Python 3\.12 in an isolated venv under ~/\.octop/\.
- A modern multi\-core CPU with a few GB of RAM is recommended for the process plus model and embedding caches, with enough disk for the database, agent workspaces, and document corpora\.
- The control plane uses SQLite by default, with PostgreSQL optional; workspace backends can include local disk, Docker sandbox, PostgreSQL, or COS/S3\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Octop Browser is a lightweight browser\-use style tool that makes an agent's browser usage more accurate and reliable\. It launches a real Chromium and communicates directly with the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) instead of routing every action through Playwright\.

## Key Features

- Direct CDP connection to a real Chromium browser without Playwright or an intermediate layer\.
- Stable ref\-based element targeting that survives layout reflows and re\-renders\.
- Token\-efficient multi\-level DOM builder that keeps prompts small\.
- Profile\-based login persistence across sessions\.
- A stateless browser\_tool with about 20 actions and a matching first\-class CLI\.
- Record and replay workflows as skill\-guided agentic execution, plus an MCP server for any MCP\-capable agent\.

## Use Cases

- Enabling AI agents to navigate, click, type, fill, and extract data from real web pages\.
- Automating browser workflows such as form filling, screenshots, tab management, and history navigation\.
- Recording a real browsing session and replaying it as skill\-guided agentic execution\.
- Exposing browser tools to any MCP\-capable agent through the built\-in MCP server\.

## Getting Started

- Install Python 3\.11 or newer and run pip install octop\-browser, then octop\-browser install\-browser to fetch a Chromium binary\.
- Use as a library with BrowserSession\.create(profile="default") or statelessly with browser\_tool(action="navigate", url=\.\.\., profile="work")\.
- Use as a CLI with commands such as octop\-browser \-\-help, octop\-browser navigate "https://example\.com" \-\-profile work, and octop\-browser dom\-tree \-\-profile work\.
- Record a workflow with octop\-browser record daemon\-start, record start, record stop, record generate\-skill, and replay run\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.11\+ (verified on 3\.11 and 3\.12)\.
- A Chromium or Chrome binary; install\-browser auto\-downloads one\.
- Optional environment configuration such as BROWSER\_USE\_MODE, BROWSER\_USE\_CDP\_WS\_URL, and BROWSER\_USE\_PROFILES\_DIR\.
- For remote or Docker Chrome, set BROWSER\_USE\_CDP\_WS\_URL to connect directly to an existing DevTools WebSocket URL and skip the launcher\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The no\-sandbox flag may be added automatically in container environments where the kernel denies unprivileged user namespaces\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Octop Gateway is a multi\-platform IM channel bridge that provides a unified message abstraction for AI agents and bots\. It connects to mainstream IM platforms and normalizes every inbound message into one processing pipeline, so agent logic is written once and runs across Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, WeCom, WeChat iLink, Yuanbao, Xiaoyi, MQTT, Telegram, and Discord\. The gateway handles transport, parsing, media, and delivery behind a common interface\.

## Key Features

- 10 platforms, one processor: Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, WeCom, WeChat iLink, Yuanbao, Xiaoyi, MQTT, Telegram, and Discord all behind one interface\.
- Unified abstraction turns each platform's quirks into a common InboundMessage and MessageEvent model\.
- Streaming events let the processor act as an async generator yielding MessageEvent for token streaming\.
- Pluggable media uses MediaBackend to store attachments, with FileSystemMediaBackend shipped by default\.
- Per\-channel constraints include rate limit, timeout, and typing indicator\.
- Push routing provides push\_text, push\_content, and push\_to\_all for proactive messages\.

## Use Cases

- Build one bot that reaches users across multiple IM platforms without writing platform\-specific code\.
- Run isolated channels for different teams or tenants from a single gateway\.
- Send proactive notifications to individual users or broadcast messages to many\.
- Connect agent logic to platforms such as Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, WeCom, Telegram, and Discord\.

## Getting Started

- Install the core library with pip install octop\-gateway\.
- For example and agent integration extras, use pip install "octop\-gateway\[examples\]"\.
- Prerequisites are Python 3\.12\+ and credentials for the platforms you connect to\.
- Copy \.env\.example to \.env for environment\-based configuration\.
- Define an async processor yielding MessageEvent, create a ChannelManager, and add platform channels\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.12\+\.
- Credentials for each platform you connect to\.
- Environment\-based configuration can be used by copying \.env\.example to \.env\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Discord integration requires enabling Message Content Intent in the developer portal\.
- QQ QR login keeps a one\-time decryption key in memory and leaves persistence of the returned channel config to the caller\.

projects.content:
## Overview

docx is a TypeScript library from Office Kit for reading, editing, and writing Word \.docx files\. It can build a document from scratch with createDocx or open an existing \.docx with openDocx, then change paragraphs, runs, lists, tables, images, headers, footers, comments, footnotes, endnotes, hyperlinks, bookmarks, and tracked changes\. It runs in Node\.js and modern browsers, and unmodeled elements are written back untouched\.

## Key Features

- Create \.docx files from scratch with createDocx and append headings, paragraphs, bullet and numbered lists, tables, inline images, headers, footers, footnotes, and a table of contents\.
- Open existing \.docx files with openDocx to replace text across the body, headers, footers, footnotes, endnotes, and comments; swap images by alt text; and accept or reject tracked insertions and deletions\.
- Render a Docx value or raw bytes into a DOM element with the companion @office\-kit/docx\-preview package in the browser\.
- Supports page setup, styles, tables, fields, comments, bookmarks, hyperlinks, core and app properties, find and replace, outline, statistics, plain\-text extraction, and validate()\.
- Uses standalone tree\-shakeable functions, ships ESM\-only with bundled \.d\.ts types, has one runtime dependency, and works in Node\.js and browsers\.

## Use Cases

- Fill a Word template by opening an existing \.docx, replacing placeholders such as \{\{name\}\}, and saving the result\.
- Generate reports, contracts, letterheads, and other structured documents programmatically from Node\.js or browser code\.
- Edit existing documents by changing text, images, headers, footers, notes, comments, or tracked changes while keeping unmodeled content intact\.
- Preview Word documents in a web page without uploading the file by using the browser preview package\.

## Getting Started

- Install with npm i @office\-kit/docx, pnpm add @office\-kit/docx, or yarn add @office\-kit/docx\.
- Import createDocx to build a document from scratch, or openDocx to open an existing \.docx template\.
- Use functions such as appendParagraph, addBulletList, addTable, setPageSize, replaceTextEverywhere, and toUint8Array to construct or modify the document\.
- For browser preview, pair the library with @office\-kit/docx\-preview and call previewToDOM\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Runs in modern browsers and Node\.js\.
- Ships ESM\-only with bundled \.d\.ts types\.
- Has no Node\-only dependencies and works in browsers, including with the Blob and File APIs\.
- One runtime dependency: fflate for ZIP handling\.
- @office\-kit/docx\-preview wraps the OSS docx\-preview renderer and runs in the browser\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is pre\-1\.0; core functions are stable but details may change before v1\.
- The library has one runtime dependency, fflate, for ZIP handling\.
- Merged table cells, nested tables, floating images, text boxes, charts, a typed API for content controls, ISO/IEC 29500 Strict files, and PDF rendering are not yet supported\.

## Overview

Office Kit's @office\-kit/pptx is a TypeScript library for reading, editing, and writing \.pptx presentation files\. It runs in Node\.js and the browser from a single ESM bundle, and preserves unknown parts like SmartArt and OLE objects on round\-trip\. The library validates output with Open XML SDK and ECMA\-376 schemas\.

## Key Features

- Read, edit, and write \.pptx files in Node\.js and the browser from a single ESM bundle\.
- Preserves unknown parts such as SmartArt, OLE objects, video, and vendor extensions on round\-trip\.
- Validates output against Open XML SDK's OpenXmlValidator and ECMA\-376 schemas in CI\.
- Supports all 16 ECMA\-376 chart plot types, shapes, tables, pictures, text, and review features\.
- Tree\-shakeable free\-function API with side\-effect\-free exports; only one runtime dependency (fflate)\.

## Use Cases

- Filling a designer\-made \.pptx template with data via token replacement or placeholder editing\.
- Editing an existing presentation from Keynote, Google Slides, or other apps and saving it back\.
- Auditing a deck: listing layouts, finding hyperlinks, or checking for empty titles\.
- Creating slides with AI using Claude Code or Codex through TSX authoring and live preview\.

## Getting Started

- Install with npm install @office\-kit/pptx\. To edit a template, load the file with loadPresentation, modify it, and save with savePresentation\. For AI\-assisted authoring, run npx \-\-yes @office\-kit/pptx\-dev@latest init my\-slides to create a project with a live preview; Node\.js

## Deployment & Requirements

- The library runs in Node\.js and modern browsers with no native modules\. The AI authoring workflow requires Node\.js 22\.18 or later and Git alongside Claude Code\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Office Kit's xlsx library reads, edits, and writes Excel \.xlsx workbooks from TypeScript in Node 22\+ and modern browsers\. It offers typed cell values, styles, formulas, charts, streaming, and byte\-for\-byte preservation of features it does not model\.

## Key Features

- Typed reading and writing for \.xlsx workbooks from bytes, files, Blob, or fetch responses, with cell values modeled as a discriminated union\.
- Write support for styles, number formats, formulas with cached values, Excel tables, data validation, conditional formatting, images, charts, and chartsheets\.
- Streaming reader and append\-only writer for large sheets, with bounded row buffering and shared\-string limits\.
- Round\-trip preservation of unmodeled parts including pivot tables, VBA projects, threaded comments, external links, and custom XML\.
- CI validation of generated OOXML against ECMA\-376 schemas plus semantic invariants\.
- Subpath imports with tree\-shakable ESM exports and no root barrel\.

## Use Cases

- Programmatically edit existing Excel reports or templates while keeping pivot tables, macros, and other unmodeled parts intact\.
- Generate large \.xlsx files with streaming writes to keep memory bounded\.
- Create typed Excel workbooks with formatting, charts, images, validation, and conditional formatting from TypeScript\.
- Read and validate uploaded \.xlsx files in Node services or browser applications with typed cell values and error classes\.

## Getting Started

- Install with pnpm add @office\-kit/xlsx or use npm, yarn, or bun\.
- Requires Node 22 or later; the package is ESM\-only and has no root barrel\.
- Load a workbook with loadWorkbook, edit cells with setCell, then save with workbookToBytes or saveWorkbook\.
- For large sheets, use createWriteOnlyWorkbook, append rows, then finalize\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node 22 or later is required; Node 18 and 20 EOL are not supported\.
- Runs in Node and modern browsers; only the @office\-kit/xlsx/node subpath touches fs, while the rest uses Web Streams, Blob, and Uint8Array\.
- The package is ESM\-only and its shipped types resolve under node16, nodenext, and bundler module resolution\.
- The full load and save path must stay under 120 KB minified and brotli\-compressed, and the streaming entry under 80 KB\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is pre\-1\.0 alpha, so APIs may shift before 1\.0; pin the version for long\-running projects\.
- Node 22 or later is required; Node 18 and 20 are EOL and not supported\.
- Only \.xlsx is supported; \.xls, \.xlsb, \.ods, and \.csv are out of scope\.
- The library has two runtime dependencies: fflate for ZIP and saxes for streaming XML\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Ollama is a tool for running open\-source large language models locally\. It supports a variety of models including Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt\-oss, Qwen, and Gemma\. With a simple CLI and REST API, you can download, run, and manage models on your own machine\.

## Key Features

- Supports a wide range of open models including Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt\-oss, Qwen, and Gemma\.
- Provides a simple CLI to run and chat with models\.
- Offers a REST API for programmatic access\.
- Includes official libraries for Python and JavaScript\.
- Available on macOS, Windows, Linux, and via Docker\.
- Can launch integrations with coding tools like Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and more\.

## Use Cases

- Coding: Use Ollama to run local models for code assistance with integrations like Claude Code and Codex\.
- AI assistant: Turn Ollama into a personal AI assistant across messaging platforms using OpenClaw\.
- Chat with models: Run and chat with models like Gemma 4 directly from the terminal\.
- REST API: Integrate Ollama into applications via its REST API for chat and model management\.

## Getting Started

- Install Ollama on macOS, Windows, or Linux using the provided install scripts, or download the installer\. For Docker, use the official image\. After installation, run 'ollama' to get started, then use 'ollama run \<model\>' to chat with a model\. See the quickstart guide for more

## Deployment & Requirements

- Ollama can be deployed on macOS, Windows, Linux, or via Docker\. It requires a compatible system with sufficient resources to run models locally\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

projects.taglineZh: 内置 IDE 的编码智能体。
projects.description: omp is a coding agent for the terminal with subagents, plan mode, LSP, DAP, memory, hashline edits, and time-traveling rules, powered by a native Rust core. Built by Stencil Labs.
projects.descriptionZh: omp 是面向终端的编码智能体，具备子智能体、计划模式、LSP、DAP、记忆、hashline 编辑和时光回溯规则，由原生 Rust 核心驱动。由 Stencil Labs 构建。
projects.content:
## Overview

omp is a terminal coding agent that ships with the IDE wired in\. It is an agentic harness built on a native Rust core, with tools tuned against real sessions, and it runs natively on macOS, Linux, and Windows without a WSL bridge\. Originally built on Mario Zechner's Pi, omp adds code execution with tool\-calling, LSP awareness, real debugger control, subagents, shared sessions, memory, and more\. It is built by Stencil Labs\.

## Key Features

- Code execution with tool\-calling: persistent Python and a Bun worker can call back into the agent's own tools over a loopback bridge\.
- LSP wired into every write, so renames route through workspace/willRenameFiles and update re\-exports, barrel files, and aliased imports\.
- Real debugger support through DAP, attaching lldb, dlv, or debugpy for breakpoints, stepping, threads, stack, and variables\.
- Time\-traveling stream rules that abort a stream on a regex match, inject the rule as a system reminder, and retry from the same point\.
- First\-class subagents: task fans out into isolated worktrees and returns schema\-validated typed results\.
- Hashline editing by content hash, plus 60\+ providers, 31 built\-in tools, 14 LSP ops, 28 DAP ops, and roughly 80k lines of Rust core\.

## Use Cases

- Driving a full coding session from the terminal, including edits, reads, searches, and shell work\.
- Debugging native, Go, or Python processes from the agent instead of adding print statements\.
- Fanning a job out across parallel subagents and reading back structured, schema\-validated results\.
- Reviewing branches, single commits, or uncommitted work with P0\-P3 priorities and a ship verdict\.

## Getting Started

- macOS and Linux: curl \-fsSL https://omp\.sh/install \| sh
- Homebrew: brew install can1357/tap/omp
- Bun (recommended): bun install \-g @oh\-my\-pi/pi\-coding\-agent
- Windows (PowerShell): irm https://omp\.sh/install\.ps1 \| iex
- Nix: nix run github:can1357/oh\-my\-pi, or nix profile install github:can1357/oh\-my\-pi

## Deployment & Requirements

- Supported platforms are macOS, Linux, and Windows\.
- Bun version 1\.3\.14 or newer\.
- On Alpine or musl, install libstdc\+\+ and libgcc first: apk add libstdc\+\+ libgcc

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The prebuilt musl binary links libstdc\+\+ and libgcc dynamically, which stock Alpine does not ship, so those packages must be installed first\.
- Several tools, including github, security\_scan, generate\_image, tts, checkpoint, rewind, and the memory tools, are setting\-gated and off by default\.

projects.taglineZh: 行级精准的 AI 代码审查命令行工具
projects.description: Open Code Review is a battle-tested AI code review CLI combining deterministic engineering with an LLM agent for precise, line-level comments. It supports multiple model providers, private data control, and built-in multi-language rules.
projects.descriptionZh: Open Code Review 是一款源自阿里巴巴内部实践的 AI 代码审查命令行工具，将确定性工程与 LLM 代理结合，读取 Git 差异并生成精确到行的结构化评论。它支持多种模型协议与私有部署，内置覆盖 40 多种语言和文件类型的审查规则。
projects.content:
## Overview

Open Code Review is an AI\-powered code review CLI that originated as Alibaba Group's internal AI code review assistant\. It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM through an agent with tool\-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line\-level precision\. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and perform deep reviews\. It also provides ocr scan for reviewing entire files when there is no meaningful diff\.

## Key Features

- Hybrid architecture separating deterministic engineering from LLM agent reasoning for file selection, bundling, rule matching, comment positioning, and scheduling\.
- Precise line\-level comment positioning with a three\-tier progressive LLM strategy and a separate reflection module to intercept hallucinations and knowledge drift\.
- Multi\-model protocol support for Anthropic Messages API, OpenAI Chat Completions API, and OpenAI Responses API, with presets including Anthropic, OpenAI, DashScope, DeepSeek, and Z\.AI, plus custom endpoints\.
- Effort\-driven progressive review with low, medium, and high depth levels that converge when a pass surfaces no new risk\.
- Smart memory compression using three\-tier frozen, compress, and active context management for deep review\.
- Built\-in review rules covering 40\+ languages and file types, including checks for NPE, thread safety, XSS, and SQL injection\.

## Use Cases

- Individual developers embedding code review into local AI\-assisted development workflows for instant feedback\.
- Platform teams integrating the tool into internal systems with control over data flow and review policies\.
- ML researchers using it as a code quality verifier in RL training pipelines to provide reward signals for code generation models\.
- Auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories through full\-file scan when there is no meaningful diff\.

## Getting Started

- Install globally with npm i \-g @alibaba\-group/open\-code\-review\.
- Verify installation with ocr version\.
- Configure a provider and model with ocr config provider and ocr config model, or use Delegation Mode\.
- Run ocr review for workspace, branch\-range, or commit reviews, or ocr scan for full\-file review\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Git 2\.41 or newer is required\.
- An LLM must be configured before reviewing code unless Delegation Mode is used\.
- The CLI is installed globally via npm\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The tool depends on Git for diff generation, code search, and repository operations\.
- The project explicitly notes lower recall than general\-purpose agents as a trade\-off favoring precision over noise\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Open Notebook is an open\-source, AI\-powered note\-taking and research platform that respects your privacy\. It combines AI with privacy controls, designed for researchers, students, and professionals\. It is an open\-source implementation of Notebook LM with more flexibility and features, supporting multi\-model AI, content integration, and podcast generation\.

## Key Features

- Privacy\-first self\-hosted: your data stays under your control with no cloud dependencies\.
- Multi\-model AI support: 18\+ providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, LM Studio, and more\.
- Multi\-modal content support: PDFs, videos, audio, web pages, Office docs, and more\.
- Professional podcast generation: advanced multi\-speaker podcasts with Episode Profiles\.
- Intelligent search and context\-aware chat: full\-text and vector search across all content, with AI conversations powered by your research\.

## Use Cases

- Research and knowledge management for researchers and professionals\.
- Learning and note\-taking for students and self\-taught learners\.
- Generating podcasts from notes for engaging content creation\.

## Getting Started

- Quick start with Docker: download docker\-compose\.yml, set your encryption key, start services with docker compose up \-d, then configure your AI provider in the UI\. See the README for full instructions\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires Docker Desktop and docker\-compose\. Uses SurrealDB as the database\. Can be deployed locally, in the cloud, or on\-premises\. Supports optional password protection for public deployments\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The encryption key must be changed from the default placeholder to secure API keys\.
- Citations are currently basic and will improve in future releases\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Open WebUI is a self\-hosted AI platform designed to be a home for AI\. It is extensible, feature\-rich, and user\-friendly, with support for Ollama and OpenAI\-compatible APIs\. It can run entirely offline and provides a provider\-agnostic interface for both local and cloud\-based models\.

## Key Features

- Effortless Setup: Install via pip, uv, Docker, or Kubernetes with official images for Ollama and CUDA\.
- Broad Model & API Integration: Connect any OpenAI\-compatible API alongside local Ollama models, including LMStudio, GroqCloud, Mistral, OpenRouter, vLLM, and more\.
- Granular RBAC & User Groups: Administrators define detailed roles, groups, and permissions for tailored access\.
- Plugin Support: Extend with Filters, Actions, Pipes, Tools, and Skills, and connect external services via MCP, MCPO, and OpenAPI tool servers\.
- Local RAG Integration: Retrieval Augmented Generation with 9 vector databases and multiple content\-extraction engines, supporting hybrid search and full\-context mode\.
- Multi\-Model Conversations: Engage several models at once to harness their individual strengths in parallel\.

## Use Cases

- Self\-hosted AI chat interface for local and cloud models\.
- Team collaboration with role\-based access and shared channels\.
- Enterprise deployment with SSO, SCIM, and production observability\.
- Building custom agents with plugins, tools, and persistent memory\.

## Getting Started

- Install via pip: pip install open\-webui, then run open\-webui serve\. For Docker, use: docker run \-d \-p 3000:8080 \-v open\-webui:/app/backend/data \-\-name open\-webui \-\-restart always ghcr\.io/open\-webui/open\-webui:main\. Access at http://localhost:3000 (or localhost:8080 with

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.11 is required for pip installation\. Docker is recommended for container deployment, with optional CUDA support requiring the Nvidia CUDA container toolkit\. Database options include SQLite (with optional encryption) or PostgreSQL, and file storage can be local or on S3,

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The :dev branch contains unstable features and may have bugs\.
- Docker installations must mount the data volume to prevent data loss\.
- Connection issues may require using \-\-network=host to reach Ollama\.
