projects.descriptionZh: OpenAI Agents SDK 是一个轻量、与提供商无关的 Python 框架，用于构建多智能体工作流。它提供智能体、任务交接、防护栏、工具、会话、追踪以及对实时和语音智能体的支持。
projects.content:
## Overview

The OpenAI Agents SDK is a production\-ready upgrade of Swarm, OpenAI's previous experimentation for agents\. It is a lightweight, Python\-first framework for building agentic AI apps with very few abstractions, including agents, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, and sandbox, realtime, and voice agent capabilities\.

## Key Features

- Agents configured with instructions, tools, guardrails, and handoffs, with a built\-in loop that continues until the task is complete\.
- Agents as tools and handoffs for delegating work across multiple agents\.
- Guardrails for input and output validation that run in parallel with agent execution\.
- Function tools, MCP server tool calling, hosted tools, and automatic schema generation with Pydantic\-powered validation\.
- Sandbox agents, realtime agents, and voice pipelines for isolated workspaces, low\-latency voice, and speech\-to\-text/agent/text\-to\-speech workflows\.
- Sessions for persistent memory and automatic conversation history, plus built\-in tracing for visualizing, debugging, and monitoring agentic workflows\.

## Use Cases

- Building multi\-agent workflows that coordinate and delegate work across multiple agents\.
- Running coding, review, or document agents inside real isolated sandbox workspaces\.
- Building low\-latency realtime voice agents and speech\-to\-text/agent/text\-to\-speech pipelines\.
- Adding guardrails, sessions, tracing, and human\-in\-the\-loop controls to agentic applications\.

## Getting Started

- Set up a Python environment with Python 3\.10 or newer\.
- Install the package with pip install openai\-agents\.
- Set the OPENAI\_API\_KEY environment variable\.
- Create an Agent with instructions and run it with Runner\.run\_sync\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.10 or newer is required\.
- Set the OPENAI\_API\_KEY environment variable before running examples\.
- For voice support, install the optional voice group with pip install 'openai\-agents\[voice\]'\.
- For Redis session support, install the optional redis group with pip install 'openai\-agents\[redis\]'\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Requires Python 3\.10 or newer\.
- The library has optional dependencies including websockets, SQLAlchemy, any\-llm, and LiteLLM for additional functionality\.
- External contributions are limited: pull requests are accepted only from repository collaborators\.

## 项目简介

OpenAI Agents SDK 是 Swarm 的生产就绪升级版，Swarm 是 OpenAI 之前对智能体的实验性项目。它是一个轻量级、Python 优先的框架，用于以极少的抽象构建智能体 AI 应用，包括智能体、任务交接、防护栏、会话、追踪以及沙盒、实时和语音智能体功能。

- Agents 配置有指令、工具、防护栏和任务交接，并带有一个持续运行直到任务完成的内置循环。
- Agents as tools 和任务交接用于在多个智能体之间委派工作。

- 构建跨多个智能体协调和委派工作的多智能体工作流。
- 在真实的隔离沙盒工作区内运行编码、审查或文档智能体。
- 构建低延迟实时语音智能体和语音转文本/智能体/文本转语音管道。

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenBot is an open\-source, fully customizable agent application for employees, running on infrastructure you own\. It is built on AG\-UI and accepts any AG\-UI endpoint as a coworker, with company knowledge, permissions, computer use, and an audit trail in one place\.

## Key Features

- A computer per Bot: each Bot gets its own container, workspace volume, and browser profile\.
- Governed tool and action gateway: every tool call is resolved, evaluated against policy, audited, and only then executed\.
- Company knowledge with real permissions: connects Google Drive and OneDrive; answers cite sources and permissions fail closed\.
- Computer use with human handoff: agents can sign in and drive interfaces while users watch, take control, and hand it back\.
- Bring your own AG\-UI agent: any AG\-UI endpoint can be registered as a Bot, on frameworks such as LangGraph, Mastra, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, or Google ADK\.
- Runs on your infrastructure: data, vectors, permissions, and conversations live in your PostgreSQL; admins supply model credentials, encrypted at rest\.

## Use Cases

- Company knowledge: answers policy and process questions from company documents and names its sources\.
- Warehouse analyst: queries the analytics warehouse and draws the answer rather than describing it\. Read\-only by construction\.
- Desk research: gathers context from the open web and drafts from it, keeping contradictory sources rather than quietly picking one\.
- Tool operator: signs in and works inside tools that have no API worth using, with the screen open so you can watch\.

## Getting Started

- Create \.env by copying \.env\.example and run bun install\.
- Run npx \-\-yes copilotkit@latest login and npx \-\-yes copilotkit@latest project select, then run bun scripts/setup\-learning\.ts\.
- Set OPENAI\_API\_KEY; generate KEY\_ENCRYPTION\_KEY with openssl rand \-base64 32\.
- Run bash scripts/start\.sh and open the app on localhost port 3010\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Docker, for PostgreSQL and the shipped Bots\.
- Bun 1\.3\+, for the app and API server\.
- A CopilotKit Intelligence project and license; a free plan is available, and Intelligence can be self\-hosted\.
- A model key\. The proof\-of\-concept Bot uses OpenAI; the LangGraph Bot can use OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google\.
- Docker Compose stands up a demo; Helm is the supported path to production\. One Docker image can carry the app, API, browser, and optionally PostgreSQL\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- OpenBot is a template rather than a hosted product, and it is not published as a package to depend on\.
- The project is alpha and under active development\.
- A CopilotKit Intelligence project and license is an external dependency, though a free plan is available and Intelligence can be self\-hosted\.
- Data and conversations are stored in the deployment's PostgreSQL, and nothing is sent to destinations you did not configure\.
- No model is bundled; the built\-in agent remains unavailable until an administrator configures a provider, with no silent fallback\.
projects.contentZh:
## 项目简介

OpenBot 是一个开源、可完全定制的智能体应用，供员工在自有基础设施上使用。它构建于 AG\-UI 之上，可将任何 AG\-UI 端点作为 AI 同事接入，并把公司知识、权限、计算机使用和审计轨迹放在一处。

## 核心功能

- 每个 Bot 拥有自己的计算机：独立容器、工作区卷和浏览器配置文件。
- 所有工具调用和操作都经过统一网关：先解析目标、按策略判定、写入审计，然后才执行。
- 公司知识库具备真实权限：可连接 Google Drive 和 OneDrive，回答会引用来源，权限不明确时不会返回结果。
- 计算机使用支持人工接管：智能体可登录并操作界面，用户可观看、接管并交还控制权。
- 可接入自有 AG\-UI 智能体：任何 AG\-UI 端点都可注册为 Bot，包括 LangGraph、Mastra、CrewAI、Pydantic AI 或 Google ADK 等框架构建的智能体。
- 在自有基础设施上运行：数据、向量、权限和对话保存在你的 PostgreSQL 中，管理员提供加密存储的模型凭据。

## 适用场景

- 公司知识：根据公司文档回答政策与流程问题，并标明来源。
- 数仓分析：查询分析数仓并画图呈现答案，而不是只做描述；按设计为只读。
- 案头研究：从开放网络收集上下文并据此起草，保留相互矛盾的来源，而不是悄悄选择其一。
- 工具操作员：登录并操作那些没有值得使用 API 的工具，屏幕保持打开以便观看。

## 快速开始

- 复制 \.env\.example 创建 \.env，并运行 bun install。
- 运行 npx \-\-yes copilotkit@latest login 和 npx \-\-yes copilotkit@latest project select，然后运行 bun scripts/setup\-learning\.ts。
- 设置 OPENAI\_API\_KEY；使用 openssl rand \-base64 32 生成 KEY\_ENCRYPTION\_KEY。
- 运行 bash scripts/start\.sh，然后在 localhost 3010 端口打开应用。

## 部署与要求

- Docker，用于 PostgreSQL 和随附的 Bot。
- Bun 1\.3\+，用于应用与 API 服务器。
- 一个 CopilotKit Intelligence 项目与许可证；提供免费方案，Intelligence 也可自托管。
- 模型密钥。概念验证 Bot 使用 OpenAI；LangGraph Bot 可使用 OpenAI、Anthropic 或 Google。
- Docker Compose 可启动演示；Helm 是受支持的生产部署路径。一个 Docker 镜像可包含应用、API、浏览器，以及可选的 PostgreSQL。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：MIT。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenClaw is an open\-source AI assistant that runs locally on your machine and works from WhatsApp, Telegram, or any chat app\. It can organize your inbox, send emails, manage your calendar, and check you in for flights\. It has no subscription, no hosted tier, and no token, and is stewarded by an independent 501(c)(3)\.

## Key Features

- Runs on your machine
- Works from WhatsApp, Telegram, or any chat app
- Organizes inbox, sends emails, manages calendar, checks in flights
- No subscription, no hosted tier, no token
- Open source, steward by 501(c)(3)
- Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux with one\-liner install or desktop apps

## Use Cases

- Personal assistant for daily tasks
- Share with your team for collaborative automation
- Run on your own hardware for privacy
- Integrate with existing chat apps

## Getting Started

- Install via one\-liner: PowerShell command for Windows, or npm i \-g openclaw\. Then run openclaw onboard\. Desktop apps are available for macOS, Windows, and Linux\. Source code can be cloned from GitHub and run with pnpm\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- macOS 15\+ for macOS app, Windows 10/11 for Windows app, Linux x64 for Linux app\. The apps and one\-liner install Node\.js and everything else\. Can also run from source with pnpm\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Linux version is marked as 'New', indicating it may be less mature than other platforms\.

## Overview

OpenCode is an open\-source AI coding agent that provides a terminal UI and a desktop app (beta)\. It includes built\-in agents for development and planning, plus a general subagent for complex tasks\.

## Key Features

- Two built\-in agents: build (full\-access) and plan (read\-only)
- General subagent for complex searches and multistep tasks
- Terminal UI
- Desktop app (beta) for macOS, Windows, and Linux
- Multiple installation methods including curl, npm, brew, scoop, choco, pacman, mise, and nix

## Use Cases

- Development work with the build agent
- Exploring unfamiliar codebases with the plan agent
- Planning changes with the plan agent
- Complex searches and multistep tasks with the general subagent

## Getting Started

- Install via the curl script or package managers such as npm, scoop, choco, brew, pacman, mise, or nix\. The desktop app can be installed via Homebrew or Scoop\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Users should remove versions older than 0\.1\.x before installing\.
- The desktop app is currently in beta\.

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenDesign is an open\-source, local\-first desktop app and a Claude Design alternative\. It makes existing coding agents the design engine for producing design artifacts from briefs\.

## Key Features

- Open\-source and local\-first: native desktop apps for macOS and Windows, with Linux available from source\.
- Agent\-native and model\-agnostic: uses coding\-agent CLIs such as DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and others, or BYOK OpenAI\-compatible endpoints\.
- Produces prototypes, live dashboards and artifacts, decks, mobile apps, documents, images, video, and HyperFrames motion graphics\.
- Sandboxed iframe preview; exports to HTML, PDF, PPTX, MP4, ZIP, or Markdown\.
- Composable plugins, functional skills, design templates, and DESIGN\.md design systems; 151 design systems ship with the repository\.
- MCP server and per\-agent install scripts expose local OpenDesign project files to compatible coding agents\.

## Use Cases

- Generate web, desktop, or mobile prototypes from a brief, plugin, and active design system\.
- Create live dashboards, decision rooms, KPI walls, and data\-rich artifacts\.
- Build decks, pitch presentations, weekly updates, and magazine\-style slides\.
- Generate images and agent\-native motion graphics or video with HyperFrames\.

## Getting Started

- Download the desktop app for macOS or Windows from the official website or GitHub Releases; after install, it auto\-detects coding\-agent CLIs and loads skills, templates, and design systems\.
- Install into a coding agent with od mcp install \<agent\>, or use the hosted install script with sh \-s \<agent\>\.
- Run with Docker: clone the repository, change to open\-design/deploy, copy \.env\.example to \.env, add OD\_API\_TOKEN, run docker compose up \-d, and open port 7456\.
- Run from source: clone the repository, enable corepack, install with pnpm install, and start the web app with pnpm tools\-dev run web\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Desktop app supports macOS Apple Silicon and Intel, and Windows x64; no prebuilt Linux artifact is currently published in official releases\.
- Docker deployment uses the deploy directory, an OD\_API\_TOKEN, and Docker Compose; browser access can use open\-design as username and the token as password\.
- Sealos App Store template runs the published Docker image with persistent workspace storage and Basic Auth on the public proxy\.
- Running from source requires Node approximately 24 and pnpm 10\.33\.x\.
- For MCP integration, DeepSeek Harness requires the official dsh CLI first; automatic MCP configuration for Claude Desktop is currently supported on macOS and Windows only\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.

## 项目简介

OpenDesign 是一个开源、本地优先的桌面应用，也是 Claude Design 的替代方案。它让现有编码智能体成为设计引擎，根据简报产出设计工件。

## 核心功能

- 开源且本地优先，提供 macOS 与 Windows 原生桌面应用，Linux 可从源码运行。
- 以智能体为核心且不绑定模型，可使用 DeepSeek Harness、Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、OpenCode 等编码智能体 CLI，也可通过 BYOK 使用 OpenAI 兼容端点。
- 可产出原型、实时仪表盘与工件、演示文稿、移动应用、文档、图像、视频和 HyperFrames 动态图形。
- 提供沙盒 iframe 预览，支持导出 HTML、PDF、PPTX、MP4、ZIP 或 Markdown。
- 采用可组合插件、功能技能、设计模板和 DESIGN\.md 设计系统，仓库内置 151 个设计系统。
- 提供 MCP 服务器和面向各智能体的安装脚本，让兼容的编码智能体读取本地 OpenDesign 项目文件。

## 适用场景

- 根据简报、插件和当前设计系统生成 Web、桌面或移动端原型。
- 创建实时仪表盘、决策室、KPI 墙和数据丰富的工件。
- 制作演示文稿、路演材料、周报和杂志风格幻灯片。
- 生成图像，并使用 HyperFrames 制作智能体原生动效或视频。

## 快速开始

- 可从官方渠道或 GitHub Releases 下载 macOS 或 Windows 桌面应用，安装后会自动检测编码智能体 CLI，并加载技能、模板和设计系统。
- 可用 od mcp install 加 agent 名称安装到编码智能体，或使用托管安装脚本 sh \-s 后接 agent 名称。
- 使用 Docker 时，克隆仓库，进入 open\-design/deploy，复制 \.env\.example 为 \.env，添加 OD\_API\_TOKEN，运行 docker compose up \-d，然后打开本地端口 7456。
- 从源码运行时，克隆仓库，启用 corepack，执行 pnpm install，再用 pnpm tools\-dev run web 启动 Web 应用。

## 部署与要求

- 桌面应用支持 macOS Apple Silicon 与 Intel，以及 Windows x64；官方发布目前未提供 Linux 预构建包。
- Docker 部署使用 deploy 目录、OD\_API\_TOKEN 和 Docker Compose；浏览器访问可使用 open\-design 作为用户名，并用令牌作为密码。
- Sealos App Store 模板运行已发布的 Docker 镜像，带持久化工作区存储，并在公共代理上启用 Basic Auth。
- 从源码运行需要 Node 约 24 和 pnpm 10\.33\.x。
- 进行 MCP 集成时，DeepSeek Harness 需要先安装官方 dsh CLI；Claude Desktop 的自动 MCP 配置目前仅在 macOS 和 Windows 上受支持。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：Apache\-2\.0。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenDots is an open\-source, self\-hostable alpha template for building always\-on AI coworkers called Dots\. Each Dot has its own role, instructions, permissions, and computer, and can work across text, calls, and Slack\. Spaces provide a home for working documents with a searchable library and visual editor, while CopilotKit human\-in\-the\-loop review cards let users approve or decline saved work\.

## Key Features

- Specialist Dots with roles, instructions, and per\-Dot permissions for browser, files, shell, and memory\.
- Dot computers using OpenBot's container supervisor, with per\-Dot browser profiles, files, shell, takeover, and action records\.
- Spaces and pages with a searchable library, visual editor, slash commands, autosave, revision checks, and Markdown source mode\.
- Conversations across text, realtime calls, and Slack, with thread history and timeline receipts\.
- Human\-in\-the\-loop review before saving drafts, with Approve & save or Decline and retry recovery\.
- Background work with recurring schedules in the original conversation, pause and retry\.

## Use Cases

- Run specialist AI coworkers for research and writing, such as a researcher investigating a topic and a writer turning findings into a draft\.
- Keep project documents in Spaces and pages, with conversations connected to specific pages\.
- Reach Dots through text, voice calls, or Slack and continue the same thread later\.
- Schedule recurring background work and let each Dot run with its own computer and permissions\.

## Getting Started

- Use Node\.js 24 and npm\.
- Clone the OpenDots repository and change into the project directory\.
- Run npm ci to install dependencies\.
- Copy \.env\.example to \.env\.
- Run npm run dev, then open the local development address at port 5173\. You can create Spaces, write pages, and configure Dots before connecting services\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js 24 and npm are required\.
- You run the application and configure its services\.
- Calls, Slack, and Dot computers each have their own setup guide\.
- Dot computers require the pinned OpenBot container supervisor and computer service; an unconfigured template does not execute commands on the host\.
- Service credentials stay on the server, and each Dot gets its own computer credential\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- OpenDots is an alpha template rather than a hosted product, so operators run and configure its services themselves\.
- Running OpenDots requires Node\.js 24 and npm, and Calls, Slack, and Dot computers each require separate setup\.
- Service credentials are kept on the server, and each Dot receives a distinct computer credential\.
- Slack and spoken compute delegation still require connected\-service verification\.
- The template is single\-owner and does not include shared editing, invitations, file uploads, or interactive page embeds\.

## 项目简介

OpenDots 是一个开源、可自托管的 alpha 模板，用于构建名为 Dot 的常驻 AI 同事。每个 Dot 拥有自己的角色、指令、权限和计算机，可在文本、通话与 Slack 中工作。Space 为工作文档提供归集空间，包含可搜索库和可视化编辑器，同时 CopilotKit 的人在回路审核卡片让用户批准或拒绝保存的工作。

## 核心功能

- 专业 Dot 具有角色、指令以及按 Dot 授予的浏览器、文件、Shell 和记忆权限。Dot 计算机使用 OpenBot 的容器监督程序，提供按 Dot 隔离的浏览器配置文件、文件、Shell、接管和操作记录。Space 与页面提供可搜索库、可视化编辑器、斜杠命令、自动保存、版本检查以及 Markdown 源码模式。对话覆盖文本、实时通话和 Slack，并保留线程历史与时间线回执。保存草稿前提供人在回路审核，可选择批准并保存或拒绝，并支持重试恢复。后台工作可在原始对话中按计划重复运行，并支持暂停和重试。

## 适用场景

- 运行负责研究和写作的专业 AI 同事，例如一个 Dot 调研主题，另一个把发现写成草稿。将项目文档保存在 Space 与页面中，并让对话与特定页面关联。通过文本、语音通话或 Slack 联系 Dot，稍后继续同一线程。安排重复后台工作，让每个 Dot 用自己的计算机和权限运行。

## 快速开始

- 使用 Node\.js 24 和 npm。克隆 OpenDots 仓库并进入项目目录。运行 npm ci 安装依赖。将 \.env\.example 复制为 \.env。运行 npm run dev，然后打开端口 5173 的本地开发地址。连接服务前即可创建 Space、编写页面并配置 Dot。

## 部署与要求

- 需要 Node\.js 24 和 npm。应用由你运行并配置其服务。通话、Slack 和 Dot 计算机各有独立设置指南。Dot 计算机需要固定版本的 OpenBot 容器监督程序和计算机服务；未配置的模板不会在主机上执行命令。服务凭据保留在服务器端，每个 Dot 获得自己的计算机凭据。

## 采用前须知

- 许可证：MIT。在使用、修改或分发项目前，请确认其具体条款。

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenHands is an AI agent platform for software development that executes real engineering work, not just suggests code\. It runs autonomous agents that plan, write, and apply changes across your codebase, helping teams complete complex tasks end\-to\-end\. Built on an open source foundation, it is designed for enterprise software development at scale\.

## Key Features

- Model\-agnostic: bring your own agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenHands) and any LLM
- Automations triggered from GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, schedules, and webhooks
- Self\-hosted or cloud deployment with secure sandboxes and full auditability
- Multi\-backend support: run agents locally, in Docker, on VMs, or in your VPC
- Agent Control Plane for centralized governance of who, what, where, and spend
- Open source core with MIT license and 89\.2K GitHub stars

## Use Cases

- Review pull requests and fix CI failures automatically
- Triage issues and open draft PRs with context
- Automate QA across the release cycle
- Investigate incidents and propose patches

## Getting Started

- Install via npm: npm install \-g @openhands/agent\-canvas
- Run agent\-canvas to start the local stack
- Optionally use Docker sandbox for isolated execution

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js 24 or later and uv for local installation
- Docker for sandboxed execution
- Can run on laptop, dedicated machine, or cloud server

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Running without a sandbox gives the agent full access to your filesystem\.
- Self\-hosting ensures your code never leaves your control\.

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenHuman is a free, open source personal AI for Mac, Windows and Linux\. It keeps data local, builds persistent memory from connected apps, and uses an orchestration engine to manage fleets of agents\. Its core is written in Rust and supports desktop, browser, and terminal clients\.

## Key Features

- Memory engine decides what to keep, compress, and surface when an agent needs context; it can mirror memory as an Obsidian vault\.
- Connects apps through OAuth, MCPs, and Skills, with support for up to 100 apps, 10,000 MCPs, and 90,000 Skills\.
- Workflows engine orchestrates agents for simple or complex automation graphs; the agent proposes workflows for review and save\.
- Runs fleets of agents in one Rust core process, with measured low marginal cost per additional agent\.
- Pluggable engines for LLM, embeddings, memory, and web search, including local models and bring\-your\-own\-key providers\.
- Ships as a desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux, plus a browser UI and terminal client\.

## Use Cases

- Use as a personal AI that lives on your laptop and learns from your connected work apps\.
- Orchestrate multiple agents to carry out tasks across tools instead of only replying in chat\.
- Automate workflows with scheduled, app\-event, or manual triggers and approval gates\.
- Build a second brain from connected apps with a local memory graph\.

## Getting Started

- Download installers from the official website or the GitHub Releases page\.
- For terminal installs, use Homebrew, Debian/Ubuntu \.deb, AUR, install scripts, and platform notes; see INSTALL\.md\.
- The desktop app runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux; browser UI and terminal client use the same core\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Desktop app supports Windows, macOS, and Linux\.
- The same core can run as a browser SPA or a terminal client\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: GPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The project is labeled an early beta and under active development\.
- Remote memory engine adapters ship, but a live install cannot yet switch to one through the host binding\.
- The Jev decision model depends on a TinyHumans credential for full behavior and falls back to BM25 without one\.

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenKnowledge is an open\-source, AI\-native markdown editor and knowledge base for humans and agents\. It combines a rich WYSIWYG markdown editing experience with desktop and web apps, optional git/GitHub sync, and built\-in MCP, skills, and agentic search for LLM wikis, second brains, and engineering documentation\.

## Key Features

- Full true WYSIWYG editing so markdown files feel like editing a Google Doc or Notion page\.
- Desktop apps for macOS, Windows, and Linux plus a web UI with file navigator, search, tabs, and graph wiki link viewer\.
- Integrated side\-by\-side AI editing with Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and other harnesses via MCP or CLI\.
- Out\-of\-the\-box MCP, skills, and agentic search for LLM wikis, second brains, and knowledge graphs\.
- No\-code team sharing and auto\-sync powered by git/GitHub\.
- Embeddable HTML and rich components such as callouts, accordions, tabs, Mermaid diagrams, images, and videos\.

## Use Cases

- Build a living knowledge base or wiki for you and your team with skills, docs, and notes in plain markdown\.
- Write engineering specs, PRDs, and roadmaps that live next to code and can be edited by humans and coding agents\.
- Create a shared second brain or agent memory that AI agents can read from and write to across sessions\.
- Maintain runbooks such as oncall guides, incident postmortems, and deployment runbooks\.

## Getting Started

- Download the desktop app for macOS, Windows, or Linux from the official OpenKnowledge download page\.
- For the web app, install the CLI with Node\.js 24\+ and git, then run ok init to scaffold the project and ok start \-\-open to serve the editor\.
- Open any existing folder on your computer that contains markdown or mdx files to begin editing\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Desktop app supports macOS Apple Silicon, Windows 10\+ x64/Arm64, and Linux x64/arm64\.
- The web app requires Node\.js 24\+ and git\.
- The app runs locally on your machine and is local\-first, private by design\.
- Git/GitHub based sync and sharing are optional\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: GPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- OpenKnowledge is local\-first and private by design, with the app running on your machine\.
- The project is open source, uses plain files that users own, and is described as self\-hostable\.
- Git/GitHub\-based sync and sharing are optional rather than required\.

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenMontage is an open\-source, agentic video production system that turns AI coding assistants into a full video production studio\. It supports research, scripting, asset generation, editing, and final composition, and can create image\-based videos, local character animation, or real\-footage documentaries\. The desktop app OpenMontage Studio provides a creative workspace where users can direct complete productions or focused tasks\.

## Key Features

- 12 production pipelines, 100\+ tools, and 700\+ agent skill and production\-knowledge files\.
- Works with AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, and Codex\.
- Local\-first composition and rendering with no watermarks and a per\-asset provenance report\.
- Can create real\-footage videos by building a CLIP\-searchable corpus from open archives and free stock sources\.
- Supports Remotion and HyperFrames composition, including captions, brand rules, and output formats such as 16:9, 1:1, and 9:16\.
- Includes an approval gate and a decision log so the production plan can be reviewed before asset work begins\.

## Use Cases

- Produce explainers, product ads, launch films, documentaries, animations, and other video formats\.
- Turn a reference YouTube video, Short, Reel, TikTok, or local clip into a grounded production plan\.
- Create a real\-footage documentary montage or stock\-footage collage from open archives and free stock sources\.
- Use existing AI coding assistants to run video editing and generation tasks from a conversation\.

## Getting Started

- Install prerequisites: Python 3\.10\+, FFmpeg, Node\.js 18\+, and an AI coding assistant such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, or Codex\.
- Clone the repository and run make setup, or use the manual setup commands for macOS/Linux or Windows PowerShell\.
- Open the project in your AI coding assistant and describe the video you want, such as a 60\-second animated explainer\.
- Add optional API keys in \.env for more image, video, music, voice, and stock media tools\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.10\+\.
- FFmpeg\.
- Node\.js 18\+\.
- An AI coding assistant such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, or Codex\.
- API keys are optional; more keys provide more tools\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- OpenMontage Studio is currently in private alpha, and beta access is waitlist\-based\.
- Capabilities vary because users bring their own media\-provider accounts and supported local tools\.
- The workflow is local\-first for footage and rendering\.
- Joining the waitlist involves email communication about the beta with an opt\-out option\.
- The website uses Google Analytics but provides an analytics opt\-out\.

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenSEO is an open\-source SEO platform and MCP server for AI agents\. It provides data and workflows for keyword research, domain overview, backlinks, rank tracking, site audits, and AI\-search visibility\. It can be used through a hosted version or self\-hosted\.

## Key Features

- Keyword research: find ideas, demand, difficulty, intent, and live SERPs\.
- Domain overview and competitor insights: estimate organic traffic and ranking keywords\.
- Backlinks: inspect backlinks, referring domains, and link quality\.
- Rank tracking: track keyword positions over time\.
- Site audit: crawl pages and surface technical issues\.
- AI visibility and Prompt Explorer: review AI mentions, citations, and prompts; compare prompts across supported AI models\.

## Use Cases

- Entrepreneurs and SEO teams can research keywords, save opportunities, and track rankings\.
- Marketers can analyze competitors, backlinks, and domain visibility\.
- AI agent users can connect agents like Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, OpenCode, or Gemini to run SEO workflows through MCP and skills\.
- Self\-hosters and developers can customize or build on OpenSEO as an open\-source alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs\.

## Getting Started

- Try the hosted version for free; no credit card required\.
- Connect an AI agent through the OpenSEO MCP server using the setup guide\.
- Set up OpenSEO Agent Skills for reusable SEO workflows\.
- For self\-hosting, follow the Docker or Cloudflare self\-hosting guides\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- A DataForSEO API key is required to retrieve SEO data\.
- Self\-hosting supports Docker for personal use/testing or Cloudflare for internet\-facing use across multiple devices or with a team; Cloudflare works on the free plan\.
- When self\-hosting, DataForSEO is paid directly\.
- Local development documentation is provided\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- OpenSEO requires an external DataForSEO API key to obtain SEO data\.
- The project recommends Cloudflare for self\-hosting unless users are already confident self\-hosting other apps, rather than Railway, Coolify, or Dokploy\.
- The hosted service charges a 28% markup on DataForSEO requests, while self\-hosting pays DataForSEO directly\.

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenUI is the open standard for generative UI\. It enables AI apps and agents to respond with interactive UI, charts, tables, forms, and dashboards\. OpenUI Lang is a compact, streaming\-first language that LLMs write to build interfaces from your own components, and it is not JSON\.

## Key Features

- OpenUI Lang is a compact, streaming\-first language that LLMs write to build interfaces from your own components; each line defines one component, such as root = Stack(\[header, chart\])\.
- Interfaces render while the response is still streaming\.
- Works with any model, any frontend framework, and any design system or component library you already use\.
- Can generate interactive UI, charts, cards, dashboards, forms, and tables\.
- The benchmark page states OpenUI Lang generates up to 3x faster and uses 67% fewer tokens than JSON\-based UI formats\.
- OpenUI is fully open source and works with your own components and design system\.

## Use Cases

- Build AI apps and agents that respond with interactive UI, charts, tables, forms, and dashboards\.
- Render dashboards, forms, tables, charts, and complete application screens from a response, not only chat messages\.
- Add OpenUI to existing agent code using integrations such as Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, LangGraph, Convex, Cloudflare, CrewAI, n8n, and Haystack without a rewrite\.
- Work within existing frontend frameworks such as React, Next\.js, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Nuxt, Remix, and Astro\.

## Getting Started

- Run pnpx @openuidev/cli@latest create to scaffold a working app\.
- Run npx @openuidev/cli@latest setup\-agent in your project to add OpenUI instructions to AGENTS\.md for coding agents such as Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code\.
- Projects created with npx @openuidev/cli@latest create already include the agent instructions\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Production deployments may need OpenUI Gateway to catch and repair invalid generated output before it reaches users\.
- Gateway can switch model providers during an outage while keeping the same model, which is an operational reliability consideration\.

projects.content:
## Overview

OpenViking is an open\-source context database for AI agents that organizes knowledge, memory, and skills as a virtual filesystem under viking://\. Agents can browse, search, and read context as files, with generated summaries and layered access\. It connects with popular agent harnesses and provides benchmarks showing improved long\-term memory accuracy and token efficiency\.

## Key Features

- One filesystem for knowledge, memory, and skills: resources, user memories, and skills each get a viking:// URI for browsing and retrieval\.
- Directory\-scoped semantic search that runs queries within project or memory subtrees instead of scanning a flat vector index\.
- Layered context with L0 abstracts, L1 overviews, and L2 full details so agents can judge relevance before reading source content\.
- Sessions become inspectable Markdown files, and ov compile can organize source material into a wiki, knowledge graph, or report\.
- Integrations with agent harnesses including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, OpenCode, and MCP clients\.
- Benchmarks report 80%\+ long\-term memory accuracy across agent frameworks and up to 63% reduction in input tokens versus baselines\.

## Use Cases

- Providing cross\-session memory for coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor through hooks, plugins, or MCP\.
- Organizing and retrieving knowledge from project documentation and GitHub repositories for retrieval\-augmented generation\.
- Improving long\-term memory accuracy and reducing token costs when connecting agent frameworks like OpenClaw, Hermes, and Claude Code\.
- Building custom agent integrations with Python, Go, or TypeScript SDKs and the HTTP API\.

## Getting Started

- Install the package with pip install openviking \-\-upgrade\.
- Run openviking\-server init to configure providers and models\.
- Run openviking\-server doctor to check configuration and connectivity\.
- Start the server with openviking\-server\.
- Use the ov CLI to add resources, run searches, and inspect context with commands like ov add\-resource, ov find, and ov grep\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Requires Python 3\.10\+ and access to an embedding model and a VLM, either cloud or local\.
- The open\-source server runs under AGPLv3 and requires no activation key; configure authentication before exposing it beyond localhost\.
- A Docker and deployment guide is available, and a desktop app beta supports macOS and Windows x64\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: AGPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The server requires an embedding model and a VLM, which can be cloud or local external dependencies\.
- The desktop app is currently in beta and limited to macOS and Windows x64\.
- The self\-managed commercial edition is activated by a license key and adds distributed deployment and official support\.

## 适用场景

## 快速开始

- 运行 openviking\-server doctor 检查配置与连通性。
- 使用 openviking\-server 启动服务。

## Overview

OpenWorker is an open\-source, local\-first AI coworker for desktop\. It runs on your machine, connects to everyday tools such as Slack, GitHub, email, calendar, and files, and carries tasks through to finished deliverables\. It ships specialist security coworkers first and checks in before consequential actions\.

## Key Features

- Runs locally on your computer as a desktop app with local secret storage for model keys and connector tokens\.
- Bring your own model: use cloud API keys, open\-weight providers, or run fully local with Ollama\.
- Works across 25\+ connectors including GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, Linear, HubSpot, Outlook, Gmail, and Google Calendar, plus terminal, local files, and MCP tools\.
- Governed actions include approval gates, standing rules, audit trails, hard floors, and an optional auto\-approve reviewer that escalates uncertainty\.
- Produces finished deliverables such as documents, spreadsheets, reports, web pages, fix pull requests, and Slack thread replies\.
- Supports scheduled automations and Slack mentions with full transcripts\.

## Use Cases

- Security review: scan code and dependencies for real risk and propose fixes that are re\-scanned and diff\-reviewed before approval\.
- Cloud posture: audit cloud configuration against common misconfiguration classes and draft the remediation plan\.
- Incident triage: gather context across tools, draft timelines, and prepare reports for security or ops incidents\.
- Everyday work and standing automations: prep customer calls, create documents, manage calendar and Slack, and run recurring briefs or reports\.

## Getting Started

- Download the macOS app for Apple Silicon\. macOS 12\+ builds are signed and notarized and auto\-update\.
- Windows 10/11 x64 builds are listed but not yet code\-signed, so SmartScreen will warn while signing is in progress\.
- Open the app, add a model key, or point it at Ollama, then ask for something real\.
- Run from source with Python 3\.10\+, Node 20\+, and the Rust toolchain via rustup\. Bootstrap the Python virtual environment, start the local agent server, and run the UI\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Desktop app: macOS 12\+ on Apple Silicon or Windows 10/11 x64\.
- Source run: Python 3\.10\+, Node 20\+, and Rust toolchain via rustup for the desktop shell\.
- Model access: bring a supported cloud provider API key or run local models via Ollama\.
- Tool connections: one\-click or manual connections, with MCP tools supported for additional integrations\.
- Optional sandbox: NVIDIA OpenShell for agent shell and file tools\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- OpenWorker is in open beta, so users should expect active polishing of rough edges\.
- Windows builds are not code\-signed, so SmartScreen warnings are expected until signing is completed\.
- Although OpenWorker is local\-first, an optional cloud account brokers OAuth handshakes for connectors\.
- Users pay model providers directly for API usage\.
- Auto\-approve reviewer verdicts are judgments, not guarantees; hard floors and the audit trail backstop them\.

projects.content:
## Overview

PaddleOCR is an OCR toolkit and document AI engine that converts PDFs and images into structured, LLM\-ready data\. It provides high\-accuracy text recognition, document parsing, and multilingual support for building intelligent RAG and Agentic applications\.

## Key Features

- Intelligent document parsing converts complex PDFs and images into Markdown or JSON, with structure\-aware conversion and fine\-grained coordinates\.
- PaddleOCR\-VL and PP\-StructureV3 support text, formula, table, chart, seal, and ancient document recognition\.
- Universal text recognition supports 100\+ languages, with PP\-OCRv6 covering 50 languages in a single model without model switching\.
- PP\-OCRv6 improves detection by 4\.6% and recognition by 5\.1% over PP\-OCRv5, with 5\.2× CPU inference speedup end\-to\-end\.
- The developer ecosystem integrates with Dify, RAGFlow, Pathway, and Cherry Studio and supports building LLM data pipelines\.
- One\-click deployment supports NVIDIA GPU, Intel CPU, Kunlunxin XPU, and diverse AI accelerators\.

## Use Cases

- Building RAG pipelines that need accurate parsing of PDFs, images, and complex documents for LLM ingestion\.
- Converting scanned documents, tables, formulas, and charts into Markdown or JSON for structured data workflows\.
- Multilingual document processing across 100\+ languages, including Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, and other scripts\.
- Embedding OCR into applications through Python, C\+\+, C\#, Java, or browser\-based inference\.

## Getting Started

- Try the online Experience Center and APIs on the official website without setup\.
- For local deployment, follow the PP\-OCR, PaddleOCR\-VL, or PP\-StructureV3 documentation based on your needs\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Python 3\.8–3\.12; OS support for Linux, Windows, and macOS; hardware support for CPU, GPU, XPU, and NPU\.
- One\-click deployment supports NVIDIA GPU, Intel CPU, Kunlunxin XPU, and diverse AI accelerators\.
- High\-performance inference supports CUDA 12 and can use Paddle Inference or ONNX Runtime backends\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Basic text recognition requires only minimal core dependencies, while document parsing and information extraction require optional dependencies\.
- High\-performance inference depends on CUDA 12 and can use Paddle Inference or ONNX Runtime backends\.
- Full support is noted for PaddlePaddle framework versions 3\.1\.0 and 3\.1\.1\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Paperclip is an open\-source app that orchestrates a team of AI agents to run a business\. It combines org charts, budgets, governance, and goal alignment in one deployment\. The platform is model\-agnostic, allowing you to bring any agent that can receive a heartbeat signal\. It looks like a task manager but under the hood handles agent coordination, cost tracking, and accountability\.

## Key Features

- Bring Your Own Agent: Any agent, any runtime, one org chart\. If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired\.
- Org Chart: Hierarchies, roles, and reporting lines for agents, giving them a boss, title, and job description\.
- Goal Alignment: Every task traces back to the organization mission, so agents know what to do and why\.
- Cost Control: Monthly budgets per agent with hard limits; agents auto\-pause at 100% utilization\.
- Ticket System: Every conversation, tool call, and decision is traced with an immutable audit log\.
- Governance: Approve hires, override strategy, pause or terminate any agent at any time\.

## Use Cases

- Running autonomous AI organizations with multiple agents across business functions\.
- Coordinating many different agents (OpenClaw, Codex, Claude, Cursor) toward a common goal\.
- Monitoring costs and enforcing budgets for AI agent operations\.
- Managing autonomous businesses from a phone or dashboard with full audit trails\.

## Getting Started

- Run \`npx paperclipai onboard \-\-yes\` to start an interactive setup that walks you through installation and creating your first agent team\. No Paperclip account is required, and no agents are installed automatically\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Paperclip is a Node\.js server with a React UI\. It can run locally with an embedded Postgres database or be deployed remotely with your own Postgres\. Self\-hosting is supported\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Security of your agents is your responsibility; Paperclip provides governance controls but does not secure your agents\.
- Bring\-your\-own\-ticket\-system is not yet available; it is on the roadmap\.
- Agents auto\-pause when they hit their budget limit, which may interrupt work until you override\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Pebrel (formerly Nebula) is a native desktop workspace that brings local shells, remote hosts, files, and AI command\-line tools together\. It is built with Rust and GPUI for Windows, macOS, and Linux and arranges terminals in tabs and splits so users can follow agent activity and read output without leaving the application\.

## Key Features

- Terminal tabs and draggable split panes with per\-pane working directories and saved workspace layouts\.
- SSH host management with saved hosts, SSH config aliases, proxy and jump\-host options, private\-key and keyboard\-interactive authentication, host\-key verification, and SFTP transfers\.
- AI CLI workflow support for Claude Code, Codex, and other recognized CLIs, with activity states, notifications tied to source panes, and captured answer reading\.
- Intelligent completion from Git repositories, project scripts, SSH config, and the filesystem, plus registered WSL distributions on Windows\.
- GPU\-accelerated GPUI interface with light and dark themes, opacity controls, eleven UI language choices, searchable settings, a command palette, and Lua configuration with validation and live reload\.
- Native Markdown document tabs and mathematical typesetting without a WebView\.

## Use Cases

- Managing local shells and remote SSH/SFTP sessions in one desktop workspace\.
- Running and monitoring Claude Code, Codex, or other AI CLIs in split panes with notifications and answer reading\.
- Using intelligent completions for Git branches, npm scripts, SSH aliases, WSL distributions, and filenames\.
- Reading Markdown documents and formulas natively alongside terminal work\.

## Getting Started

- Choose a package from the latest release\.
- On Windows, run the installer or extract the ZIP and launch pebrel\.exe while keeping the bundled directories together\.
- On Linux, install the DEB or make the AppImage executable\. On macOS, open the matching DMG and drag Pebrel into Applications\.
- For configuration, run pebrel config init \-\-language en\-US and pebrel config check\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Windows 10 1809\+ or 11 on x64; installer \.exe and portable \.zip packages are provided\.
- Linux Preview on x64 with glibc 2\.35\+; AppImage, \.deb, and portable \.tar\.gz packages are provided\.
- macOS Preview with deployment target 14\+ on Apple Silicon/arm64 or Intel/x64; \.dmg packages are provided\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: GPL\-3\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Restoring an AI conversation after the process exits depends on a supported CLI and a usable session identity\.
- Image attachment previews for AI CLIs depend on the CLI itself\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Pele is a lightweight open source library developed for Obsidian that renders Mermaid diagrams to SVG\. It is synchronous, has no runtime dependencies, and uses CSS variables for colors and fonts\. Pele supports every diagram type built into Mermaid 12\.1\.0\.

## Key Features

- Renders Mermaid syntax to SVG and supports every diagram type built into Mermaid 12\.1\.0\.
- Themes diagrams with CSS variables for colors and fonts; color changes apply without re\-rendering\.
- Has zero runtime dependencies and a 230 kB gzip bundle, compared with 1\.6 MB for Mermaid\.js\.
- Adapts diagram layout to small screens and container width when mounted in a browser\.
- Provides render(), mount(), renderAsync(), and individual diagram registration for bundle control\.
- Escapes diagram text, filters links and styles, and limits source and output size\.

## Use Cases

- Render Mermaid diagrams in web apps by passing Mermaid syntax to render() and inserting the returned SVG\.
- Mount diagrams into browser elements with mount(), which reads fonts from CSS and adapts layout to container width\.
- Match an application or editor theme by setting CSS variables on the diagram or a parent element\.
- Render diagrams quickly in Obsidian and match the app theme\.

## Getting Started

- Install Pele with npm install pele, pnpm add pele, yarn add pele, or bun add pele\.
- Alternatively, load the browser build from a CDN with a script tag\.
- Import render from pele, pass Mermaid syntax to render(), and insert the returned svg into the page\.
- In a browser, use mount() to render into an element, read fonts from CSS, and adapt layout to the container width\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Install from npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun, or load Pele from a CDN in the browser\.
- The library has no runtime dependencies\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Pele targets Mermaid 12\.1\.0 syntax but uses its own layout and visual style, so output may differ from Mermaid\.js\.
- Handling untrusted diagrams requires following Pele's security guidance for errors and icons\.

projects.content:
## Overview

PhotoCraft is an open\-source image editor and clean\-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop, rebuilt in pure Rust\. It is a native, offline application with layers, masks, adjustment layers, layer styles, type, vectors, brushes, and real layered PSD files\. It runs on macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, and Web\.

## Key Features

- Familiar menus, shortcuts, panels, and tools designed to be productive on day one\.
- Native GPU canvas rendering on Metal, Vulkan, DirectX 12, and WebGPU, with no Electron or web view\.
- Real layered files: opens and saves layered PSD and PSB documents\.
- Non\-destructive editing with 16 adjustment layers, more than 70 live\-preview filters, smart objects, smart filters, and layer styles\.
- On\-device selection tools for subjects and objects, with mask refinement that runs on your machine\.
- Serious color support for 8, 16, and 32\-bit documents in RGB, CMYK, Lab, and Grayscale, with ICC color management and soft proofing\.

## Use Cases

- Editing and retouching photos with layers, masks, adjustment layers, and live\-preview filters\.
- Compositing and design work using type, vector shapes, layer styles, and smart objects\.
- Opening and saving layered PSD and PSB documents for Photoshop\-compatible workflows\.
- Exporting images with format, quality, transparency, and scale controls, plus one\-click PNG quick export\.

## Getting Started

- Download a standalone installer for macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, or the self\-hosted web build\.
- Install the ArtCraft Launcher to install PhotoCraft and keep it updated alongside other Crafting Apps\.
- To build from source, install Rust 1\.90 or newer, clone the repository, and run cargo run \-\-release \-p photocraft\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Build from source requires Rust 1\.90 or newer\.
- Native builds are available for macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, and Web\.
- Linux Flatpak is sandboxed and can be installed with flatpak install \-\-user\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- PhotoCraft is presented as an early\-alpha product\.
- The recommended installation route depends on the ArtCraft Launcher\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Pi is an AI agent toolkit that provides a unified LLM API, an agent loop, a terminal UI, and a coding agent CLI\. It includes multiple packages for building agents, telemetry, durable runtimes, and more\.

## Key Features

- Unified multi\-provider LLM API supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others
- Agent runtime with tool calling and state management
- Interactive coding agent CLI
- Terminal UI library with differential rendering
- Durable conversation, task, and document runtime

## Use Cases

- Building custom AI agents with tool calling and state management
- Using the interactive coding agent for development tasks
- Creating terminal\-based AI applications
- Implementing durable conversation and task systems

## Getting Started

- For development, run \`npm install \-\-ignore\-scripts\` to install dependencies, then \`npm run build\` to build all packages\. Use \`\./test\.sh\` to run tests, and \`\./pi\-test\.sh\` to run pi from sources\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Pi can be containerized or sandboxed for stronger boundaries\. See the containerization documentation for patterns using Gondolin, Docker, or OpenShell\. Standalone binaries can be built from release source archives using the provided build script\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Pi does not include a built\-in permission system; it runs with the permissions of the launching user and process\.
- New issues and PRs from new contributors are auto\-closed by default, with maintainers reviewing them daily\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Plannotator is a locally running tool for reviewing and annotating plans and code produced by AI coding agents\. It intercepts plan approval steps, provides a diff viewer for agent\-written code, and sends structured feedback back to the agent\. It also includes agent skills for HTML artifacts, wireframes, interactive prototypes, plans, and diagrams\.

## Key Features

- Plan review: automatically hooks into the agent's plan step so you can annotate plans before they run\.
- Code review: PR\-style diff viewer for local diffs or GitHub/GitLab PRs, with side\-by\-side or unified view and line\-level annotations\.
- Runs locally with review data staying local by default; no usage telemetry or analytics\.
- Version history saves every plan revision with diffs between versions, and draft auto\-save preserves annotations across server crashes and restarts\.
- Link sharing uses URL fragments for small shares and encrypted short links for larger and HTML shares\.
- Integrations for VS Code, Obsidian, Bear, and GitHub PRs, plus commands like /plannotator\-annotate, /plannotator\-review, and /plannotator\-last\.

## Use Cases

- Review an agent's proposed plan before execution: annotate inline, mark deletions, add comments or replacements, then approve or deny with structured feedback\.
- Review agent\-written code before committing: run /plannotator\-review to see uncommitted changes in a diff viewer, add line\-level suggestions, and stage or unstage files\.
- Share annotated plans and code feedback with a team using local data, link sharing, or the hosted Workspaces layer\.
- Annotate the agent's last message or any markdown, spec/plan, folder, or URL using /plannotator\-annotate or /plannotator\-last\.

## Getting Started

- Install Plannotator locally with: curl \-fsSL https://plannotator\.ai/install\.sh \| bash
- In Claude Code, add the marketplace with /plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator, install with /plugin install plannotator@plannotator, then restart Claude Code to activate hooks\.
- Use /plannotator\-annotate \<file\|dir\|url\> to annotate any markdown, spec/plan, folder, or URL and send feedback\.
- Use /plannotator\-review \[PR\_URL\] for code review of local diffs or GitHub/GitLab pull requests\.
- Use /plannotator\-last to annotate the agent's last message\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Runs locally\.
- Integrates with Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, Codex, and VS Code; works with any agent that supports plan mode\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Review data stays local by default, with no usage telemetry or analytics\.
- Link sharing uses URL fragments for small shares and encrypted short links for larger and HTML shares\.
- Draft auto\-save preserves annotations across server crashes and restarts\.

## Overview

Promptfoo is a CLI and library for evaluating and red\-teaming LLM\-based applications\. It supports automated evaluations of prompts and models, red teaming and vulnerability scanning, model comparisons, CI/CD checks, code scanning, and sharing results with a team\. It is open source and MIT licensed\.

## Key Features

- Automated evaluations for prompts, models, and RAG pipelines
- Red teaming and vulnerability scanning for LLM applications
- Side\-by\-side comparison of model providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, and Ollama
- CI/CD integration and code scanning for LLM\-related security and compliance issues in pull requests
- Local execution for LLM evals so prompts do not leave your machine
- Declarative configs with command line and library usage

## Use Cases

- Test and improve prompts, agents, and RAGs with automated evaluations
- Secure AI applications with red teaming and vulnerability scanning
- Compare model performance across providers
- Add automated LLM checks to CI/CD and review pull requests for security and compliance issues

## Getting Started

- Install with npm install \-g promptfoo, or use brew install promptfoo, pip install promptfoo, or npx promptfoo@latest\.
- Run promptfoo init \-\-example getting\-started\.
- Set an API key for most LLM providers as an environment variable, for example export OPENAI\_API\_KEY=sk\-abc123\.
- Run promptfoo eval and promptfoo view in the getting\-started directory\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Can be installed via npm, Homebrew, pip, or run with npx\.
- Most LLM providers require an API key set as an environment variable\.
- Supports on\-premise or cloud integration\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Most LLM providers require an API key configured as an environment variable\.
- LLM evaluations can run locally and are described as private\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine and vector database written in Rust\. It provides a production\-ready service with an API to store, search, and manage points, which are vectors with an additional payload\. Qdrant is tailored for extended filtering support, making it useful for neural\-network or semantic\-based matching, faceted search, and other applications\.

## Key Features

- Dense, sparse, and multi vector search, including late interaction models such as ColBERT\.
- Filtering on JSON payload with keyword matching, full\-text search, numeric ranges, geo\-locations, and should, must, and must\_not clauses\.
- Hybrid search combining multiple vectors in a single query with configurable fusion strategies like Reciprocal Rank Fusion and Distribution\-Based Score Fusion\.
- Vector quantization and on\-disk storage to reduce RAM usage and tune the trade\-off between search speed and precision\.
- Distributed deployment with sharding and replication, plus zero\-downtime collection updates and resizing\.
- REST and gRPC APIs, official client libraries for multiple languages, and a Web UI for exploring collections and monitoring deployment health\.

## Use Cases

- Semantic text search that finds meaningful connections in short texts beyond keyword\-based search\.
- Similar image search, such as visual food discovery where users find meals by appearance rather than names or ingredients\.
- Extreme classification, including e\-commerce product categorization with millions of labels\.
- Recommendation, discovery, and faceted search across neural\-network or semantic\-based matching applications\.

## Getting Started

- Run the Qdrant container locally with docker run \-p 6333:6333 qdrant/qdrant\.
- Connect to the server with a client, for example Python using qdrant\_client\.QdrantClient with url http://localhost:6333\.
- Use the Quick Start Guide, detailed documentation, and the Qdrant Essentials course for further setup\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- The local Docker command starts an insecure deployment without authentication, open to all network interfaces, so the instance should be secured\.
- Before deploying Qdrant to production, review the installation and security guides\.
- Qdrant is also available as a fully managed Qdrant Cloud service, including a free tier\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The default local container deployment is insecure: it lacks authentication and is open to all network interfaces\.

projects.content:
## Overview

QMD is an on\-device search engine for retrieving content from markdown notes, meeting transcripts, documentation, and knowledge bases\. It supports keyword and natural language search with BM25 full\-text search, vector semantic search, and LLM re\-ranking, all running locally via node\-llama\-cpp with GGUF models\.

## Key Features

- Hybrid search combines BM25 full\-text search, vector semantic search, and LLM re\-ranking\.
- Runs locally on\-device using node\-llama\-cpp and GGUF models\.
- Indexes collections of markdown notes, meeting transcripts, documentation, and knowledge bases\.
- Supports keyword and natural language queries through search, vsearch, and query commands\.
- Provides an MCP server with query, get, multi\_get, and status tools for agent integration\.
- Offers a Node\.js and Bun SDK for embedding search in applications\.

## Use Cases

- Search personal notes, meeting transcripts, documentation, and knowledge bases from the command line\.
- Feed structured search results to AI agents and LLM workflows via JSON and file output\.
- Add local document retrieval to Node\.js or Bun applications with the SDK\.
- Enable MCP clients such as Claude Desktop or Claude Code to query local indexed content\.

## Getting Started

- Install globally with npm install \-g @tobilu/qmd or bun install \-g @tobilu/qmd, or run directly with npx @tobilu/qmd or bunx @tobilu/qmd\.
- Create collections for notes, docs, and meeting transcripts using qmd collection add, then add context with qmd context add\.
- Generate embeddings with qmd embed, and search using qmd search for keywords, qmd vsearch for semantic search, or qmd query for hybrid search with reranking\.
- Configure an MCP client to run qmd mcp, or start the HTTP transport with qmd mcp \-\-http\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Node\.js version 22 or higher\.
- Bun version 1\.0\.0 or higher\.
- On macOS, Homebrew SQLite for extension support\.
- Local GGUF models are auto\-downloaded on first use from HuggingFace and cached; default models include embeddinggemma\-300M\-Q8\_0, qwen3\-reranker\-0\.6b\-q8\_0, and qmd\-query\-expansion\-1\.7B\-q4\_k\_m\.
- The embedding model requires re\-indexing with qmd embed \-f when switching models, because vectors are not cross\-compatible\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- The HTTP MCP server is unauthenticated, so users must add their own authentication before exposing it off\-host\.
- AST\-aware chunking depends on optional tree\-sitter grammars\.
- MCP tool parameters are not strictly validated, so unknown parameters are silently ignored\.

- 通过 node\-llama\-cpp 与 GGUF 模型在设备端本地运行。
- 可索引 markdown 笔记、会议记录、文档和知识库的集合。
- 通过 search、vsearch 和 query 命令支持关键词与自然语言查询。

- 通过 JSON 和文件输出将结构化搜索结果提供给 AI 智能体和 LLM 工作流。
- 使用 SDK 为 Node\.js 或 Bun 应用添加本地文档检索。
- 让 Claude Desktop 或 Claude Code 等 MCP 客户端查询本地已索引内容。

## 快速开始

- 使用 npm install \-g @tobilu/qmd 或 bun install \-g @tobilu/qmd 全局安装，也可用 npx @tobilu/qmd 或 bunx @tobilu/qmd 直接运行。

projects.content:
## Overview

Qwen3 is the large language model series developed by the Qwen team at Alibaba Cloud\. It includes dense and Mixture\-of\-Experts models in sizes from 0\.6B to 235B\-A22B, along with Qwen3\-2507 updates in Instruct and Thinking variants\. The series supports thinking and non\-thinking modes for reasoning and chat, multilingual use, long\-context understanding, and deployment or local execution across multiple frameworks\.

## Key Features

- Dense and Mixture\-of\-Experts models in sizes including 0\.6B, 1\.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B, 32B, 30B\-A3B, and 235B\-A22B\.
- Qwen3\-2507 provides Instruct and Thinking variants in 235B\-A22B, 30B\-A3B, and 4B sizes\.
- Switching between thinking mode for complex logical reasoning, math, and coding, and non\-thinking mode for efficient general\-purpose chat\.
- Support for 100\+ languages and dialects with multilingual instruction following and translation\.
- Long\-context understanding of 256K tokens, extendable up to 1 million tokens for Qwen3\-2507\.
- Agent capabilities for precise integration with external tools and complex agent\-based tasks\.

## Use Cases

- Complex logical reasoning, mathematics, science, and coding tasks\.
- Efficient general\-purpose chat, creative writing, role\-playing, and multi\-turn dialogue\.
- Multilingual instruction following and translation across 100\+ languages and dialects\.
- Tool use and complex agent\-based tasks requiring integration with external tools\.

## Getting Started

- Install Transformers with transformers\>=4\.51\.0, load a Qwen3 checkpoint with AutoModelForCausalLM and AutoTokenizer, apply the chat template, and generate text\.
- ModelScope is recommended for users in mainland China and provides a Python API similar to Transformers plus the modelscope download CLI\.
- Other local run options include llama\.cpp, Ollama, LMStudio, ExecuTorch, MNN, MLX LM, and OpenVINO\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- Transformers\>=4\.51\.0 is required for Transformers usage, and the latest version is recommended\.
- SGLang\>=0\.4\.6\.post1 is required for SGLang serving\.
- vLLM\>=0\.9\.0 is recommended for vLLM serving\.
- TensorRT\-LLM\>=0\.20\.0rc3 is recommended for TensorRT\-LLM serving\.
- llama\.cpp\>=b5401 is recommended for full Qwen3 support\.

## Before You Adopt

- No recognizable license was detected; verify permission to use, modify, and distribute the project before adoption\.
- Qwen3\-Instruct\-2507 only supports non\-thinking mode\.
- Qwen3\-Thinking\-2507 only supports thinking mode\.
- Ollama naming may not be consistent with Qwen original naming\.
- Ollama default context and prediction settings can cause trouble for Qwen3 models\.
- SGLang and vLLM may have suboptimal multi\-step tool use quality with Qwen3 thinking models due to dropped reasoning content; the suggested workaround is to pass content as\-is while fixes are pending\.

projects.content:
## Overview

Qwen3\-VL is the multimodal large language model series developed by Qwen team, Alibaba Cloud\. It delivers comprehensive upgrades in text understanding and generation, visual perception and reasoning, extended context length, spatial and video dynamics comprehension, and agent interaction capabilities\. It is available in Dense and MoE architectures that scale from edge to cloud, with Instruct and reasoning\-enhanced Thinking editions\.

## Key Features

- Visual Agent: Operates PC/mobile GUIs—recognizes elements, understands functions, invokes tools, completes tasks\.
- Visual Coding Boost: Generates Draw\.io/HTML/CSS/JS from images/videos\.
- Advanced Spatial Perception: Judges object positions, viewpoints, and occlusions; provides stronger 2D grounding and enables 3D grounding\.
- Long Context & Video Understanding: Native 256K context, expandable to 1M; handles books and hours\-long video with full recall and second\-level indexing\.
- Expanded OCR: Supports 32 languages (up from 10); robust in low light, blur, and tilt; better with rare/ancient characters and jargon\.
- Enhanced Multimodal Reasoning: Excels in STEM/Math—causal analysis and logical, evidence\-based answers\.

## Use Cases

- Omni recognition for animals, plants, people, scenic spots, cars, and merchandise\.
- Document parsing with layout position information and Qwen HTML format\.
- Video understanding including video OCR, long video understanding, and video grounding\.
- Mobile and computer\-use agents for GUI control\.

## Getting Started

- Install transformers version 4\.57\.0 or later: pip install "transformers\>=4\.57\.0"\.
- Use ModelScope for checkpoint downloads, especially recommended for users in mainland China\.
- Load models such as Qwen3\-VL\-235B\-A22B\-Instruct with Transformers AutoModelForImageTextToText and AutoProcessor, then apply the chat template for inference\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Requires transformers version 4\.57\.0 or later\.
- Users in mainland China are advised to use ModelScope for downloading checkpoints\.

## 项目简介

Qwen3\-VL 是 Qwen 团队（阿里巴巴云）开发的多模态大语言模型系列。它在文本理解与生成、视觉感知与推理、扩展上下文长度、空间与视频动态理解以及智能体交互能力等方面进行了全面升级。它提供从边缘到云端的密集和 MoE 架构，并有 Instruct 和推理增强的 Thinking 版本。

## 核心功能

- Visual Agent：操作 PC/移动 GUI——识别元素、理解功能、调用工具、完成任务。
- Visual Coding Boost：从图像/视频生成 Draw\.io/HTML/CSS/JS。
- Advanced Spatial Perception：判断物体位置、视角和遮挡；提供更强的 2D 定位并支持 3D 定位。
- Long Context & Video Understanding：原生 256K 上下文，可扩展至 1M；处理书籍和数小时视频，具备完整回忆和秒级索引。
- Expanded OCR：支持 32 种语言（从 10 种升级）；在低光、模糊和倾斜下稳健；更好地处理稀有/古代字符和术语。
- Enhanced Multimodal Reasoning：擅长 STEM/数学——因果分析和基于逻辑、证据的答案。

## 适用场景

- 全识别：识别动物、植物、人物、景点以及汽车和商品等各种物体。
- 文档解析：包含布局位置信息和 Qwen HTML 格式。
- 视频理解：包括视频 OCR、长视频理解和视频定位。
- 移动端和计算机使用代理：用于 GUI 控制。

## 快速开始

- 安装 transformers 4\.57\.0 或更高版本：pip install "transformers\>=4\.57\.0"。
- 使用 ModelScope 下载检查点，尤其推荐中国大陆用户使用。
- 使用 Transformers 的 AutoModelForImageTextToText 和 AutoProcessor 加载 Qwen3\-VL\-235B\-A22B\-Instruct 等模型，然后应用聊天模板进行推理。

## 部署与要求

- 需要 transformers 4\.57\.0 或更高版本。

projects.name: REA

projects.taglineZh: 用你的编程智能体进行逆向工程
projects.description: REA gives coding agents tools for reverse engineering. Ask about an app, game, or website, and it returns code, references, and runtime observations so your agent can explain behavior and help rebuild a feature.
projects.descriptionZh: REA 为编程智能体提供逆向工程工具。你可以询问某个应用、游戏或网站，它会返回代码、引用与运行时观察结果，让智能体解释其行为并协助重建功能。
projects.content:
## Overview

REA is an MCP\-based toolset for reverse engineering with coding agents\. It connects an agent to tools that inspect native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, \.NET assemblies, websites, Android packages, firmware, and other targets\. Analysis runs locally, and results include evidence and limitations\.

## Key Features

- Connects coding agents through MCP to inspect targets and trace relevant code\.
- Supports native binary analysis with Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA, returning pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls, and references\.
- Analyzes JavaScript and Electron applications, including modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC, and native add\-on relationships\.
- Covers many targets such as \.NET assemblies, Android APKs and devices, websites, firmware, saved network captures, SQLite databases, recorded packets, and process behavior\.
- Runs analysis locally and returns findings with the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion\.

## Use Cases

- Explain how a feature in an app, game, or website works by having an agent inspect the target and trace the code behind it\.
- Recover logic from a binary or application and build a version of the feature for your own project\.
- Investigate native binaries to examine functions, strings, references, and call relationships in executables and libraries\.
- Follow runtime behavior through browser or process activity and compare results across runs\.

## Getting Started

- Install Node\.js and npm, then run npx rea\-agents@latest setup in your terminal\.
- Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, approve them, and restart your agent afterward\.
- Ask your agent to inspect a target, for example: Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project\.
- Use terminal commands such as npx \-y rea\-agents@latest analyze\-javascript\-application /absolute/path/to/app \-\-json\.
- To install the rea command for regular use, run npm install \-\-global rea\-agents and then rea \-\-help\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- REA requires Node\.js 22\.x (\>=22\.19), 24\.x (\>=24\.11), or 26\+, plus npm\.
- Native binary analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval\.
- Static JavaScript and Electron analysis needs Node\.js and npm; on Linux it requires a procps\-compatible ps on REA's PATH for process ownership checks\.
- Other targets may require caller\-supplied tools such as JADX and a full JDK for Android APKs, adb for Android devices, Binwalk or Unblob for firmware, TShark 4\.x for recorded packets, or pwntools for offline ELF layout and recorded Linux crashes\.
- Static JavaScript and \.NET inspection read supplied files without running the application\. Runtime capture runs or interacts with the selected target using your user permissions\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: MIT\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- A similar repository name or copied README does not establish that a download is official\.
- REA requires Node\.js 22\.x (\>=22\.19), 24\.x (\>=24\.11), or 26\+, plus npm\.
- Native binary analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval\.

## 项目简介

REA 是一套基于 MCP 的逆向工程工具集，供编程智能体使用。它把智能体连接到可检查原生二进制、JavaScript 与 Electron 应用、\.NET 程序集、网站、Android 包、固件等多种目标的工具。分析在本地运行，结果会附带证据与局限。

## 核心功能

- 通过 MCP 连接编程智能体，检查目标并追踪相关代码。
- 原生二进制分析可配合 Hopper、Ghidra 或 IDA，返回伪代码、汇编、字符串、符号、调用与引用。
- 分析 JavaScript 与 Electron 应用，涵盖模块、导入、source map、路由、IPC 与原生插件关系。
- 覆盖 \.NET 程序集、Android APK 与设备、网站、固件、已保存的网络抓包、SQLite 数据库、录制的数据包以及进程行为等目标。
- 分析在本地运行，每项结论都附带证据与局限。

- 让智能体检查某个应用、游戏或网站，并追踪其背后的代码，解释该功能是如何工作的。

- 调查原生二进制，查看可执行文件与库中的函数、字符串、引用和调用关系。
- 通过浏览器或进程活动跟踪运行时行为，并比较多次运行的结果。

## 快速开始

- 安装 Node\.js 与 npm，然后在终端运行 npx rea\-agents@latest setup。
- 选择要接入的智能体，检查它提出的更改并批准，随后重启你的智能体。
- 让智能体检查某个目标，例如：了解 Notes 应用中的搜索是如何工作的，向我展示证据，并为我的项目构建类似功能。
- 也可以使用终端命令，例如 npx \-y rea\-agents@latest analyze\-javascript\-application /absolute/path/to/app \-\-json。
- 若要安装常用的 rea 命令，运行 npm install \-\-global rea\-agents，然后运行 rea \-\-help。

## 部署与要求

- REA 需要 Node\.js 22\.x（\>=22\.19）、24\.x（\>=24\.11）或 26\+，以及 npm。
- 原生二进制分析可使用现有的 Hopper、Ghidra 或 IDA 安装；setup 可在获得批准后选择安装 Hopper。
- 静态 JavaScript 与 Electron 分析需要 Node\.js 和 npm；在 Linux 上还需要 REA 的 PATH 中有兼容 procps 的 ps，用于进程归属检查。

- 静态 JavaScript 与 \.NET 检查只读取提供的文件，不运行应用。运行时捕获会以你的用户权限运行或与所选目标交互。

projects.content:
## Overview

Recordly is an open\-source desktop app for recording and editing screen captures with motion\-driven presentation tools built in\. It runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux, combining platform\-specific capture with a renderer\-driven editor and export pipeline for demos, walkthroughs, and product videos\.

## Key Features

- Automatic zoom suggestions, smooth cursor movement, motion effects, and styled frames with wallpapers, colors, gradients, blur, padding, and shadows\.
- Dynamic webcam bubble overlays with positioning, mirroring, shadow, roundness, and optional zoom\-reactive scaling\.
- Drag\-and\-drop timeline editing for zooms, trims, speed regions, annotations, audio regions, and crop\-aware edits, with projects saved as \.recordly files\.
- Recording of an entire display or a single app window, with microphone and system audio capture and native capture backends where supported\.
- MP4 and GIF export with quality, frame\-rate, loop, size, aspect ratio, and output dimension controls\.
- Community\-driven extensions and a marketplace for cursor click sounds, device frames, browser mockups, wallpapers, render hooks, and settings panels\.

## Use Cases

- Creating product demos and walkthroughs\.
- Recording tutorials and educational videos\.
- Producing quick social posts as MP4 or looping GIF\.
- Adding polish to raw screen captures without a motion designer\.

## Getting Started

- Download a prebuilt release for macOS, Windows, or Linux\.
- On Arch Linux or Manjaro, install the recordly\-bin package from the AUR with yay \-S recordly\-bin\.
- To build from source, clone the repository, run npm install, then npm run dev; use npm run build for packaged builds\.
- On macOS, if a locally built app is quarantined, remove the quarantine flag with xattr \-rd com\.apple\.quarantine /Applications/Recordly\.app\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- macOS 14\.0 (Sonoma) or later\.
- Windows 10 20H1 (Build 19041, May 2020) or later for the native Windows Graphics Capture helper and best cursor\-hiding behavior\.
- Linux on modern distros; system audio generally requires PipeWire\.
- macOS build from source requires Xcode Command Line Tools\.
- Linux Ubuntu/Debian build from source requires build\-essential, cmake, libx11\-dev, libxtst\-dev, libxrandr\-dev, and libxt\-dev\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Other\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- On Linux, cursor hiding is not currently supported through Electron desktop capture\.
- On Linux, enabling the rendered cursor overlay while using Electron desktop capture may result in exports showing both the real cursor and the styled cursor\.
- On Windows builds older than 19041, recording can fall back to Electron capture and the real OS cursor may remain visible in recordings\.
- System audio support varies by platform, and Linux system audio generally requires PipeWire\.
- Locally built macOS apps may be quarantined by macOS\.

projects.name: Rerun
projects.tagline: The data layer for physical AI. From collection to training.
projects.taglineZh: 面向物理 AI 的数据层，覆盖从采集到训练
projects.description: Rerun is the data layer for physical AI, with an open source SDK to log, query, visualize, and stream multimodal robotics data from collection to training.
projects.descriptionZh: Rerun 是面向物理 AI 的数据层，提供开源 SDK，用于记录、查询、可视化和流式传输多模态机器人数据，贯穿从采集到训练的全流程。
projects.content:
## Overview

Rerun is the data layer for physical AI\. It ingests multi\-rate, multimodal data such as images, point clouds, transforms, time series, joint states, and video from robot logs, human\-data rigs, simulation, and web video\. The built\-in viewer renders everything in sync and in realtime, while the same data can be queried with dataframes or SQL and streamed directly into training\. It is built in Rust on column\-chunk storage purpose\-built for multi\-rate physical data, with SDKs in Python, Rust, and C\+\+\.

## Key Features

- Log, query, visualize, and stream multimodal robotics data with an open source SDK\.
- Visualize multi\-rate, multimodal sequences in sync and in realtime with a time\-aware built\-in viewer\.
- Query recordings with full dataframe or SQL queries down to columns, time ranges, and values\.
- Store multi\-rate, multimodal data as column\-chunks in rrd files, and ingest from formats such as MCAP, rrd, and LeRobot\.
- Stream dataset mixes directly to training without an export step, using a column\-aware and video\-codec\-aware dataloader\.
- Rerun Hub provides catalog, byte\-range indexing, retrieval, query, transform, train, and team sharing infrastructure for Rerun data\.

## Use Cases

- Debugging robotics systems by visualizing RGB camera feeds, depth images, lidar scans, segmentation outputs, 3D maps, detected objects, and confidence over time\.
- Running computer vision pipelines such as SLAM, hand tracking, and motion retargeting as table edits\.
- Querying raw, intermediate, and derived data with dataframes or SQL to build datasets for training and evaluation\.
- Streaming dataset mixes directly to GPUs for training without export jobs or stale copies\.

## Getting Started

- Install the Python SDK with pip install rerun\-sdk\.
- Add the Rust SDK with cargo add rerun\.
- Install the Rerun Viewer binary to stream log data over the network or load \.rrd data files; it can be installed with pip install rerun\-sdk or cargo install rerun\-cli \-\-locked \-\-features nasm\.
- Run the Rerun Viewer in a browser, or follow the C\+\+, Python, or Rust quick start guides\.

## Deployment & Requirements

- To stream log data over the network or load \.rrd data files, install the rerun binary\.
- Only the Python SDK comes bundled with the Viewer; C\+\+ and Rust rely on a separate Viewer install\.
- The nasm Cargo feature requires the nasm CLI to be installed and available in your path; skipping it may result in inferior video decoding performance\.
- The Rerun Viewer can run in a web browser\.

## Before You Adopt

- License: Apache\-2\.0\. Review its terms before using, modifying, or distributing the project\.
- Rerun is in active development and the API is still evolving, so breaking changes should be expected\.
- Viewer performance can degrade when there are too many entities\.
- Multi\-million point clouds can be slow\.
- Rerun Hub, the scalable catalog for robotic data, is currently available only for a few select design partners\.
